acceptance.given: a delivered capability's openai face, which counts no tokens, and the capability gateway routing to it as the workload of the capability's name
acceptance.when: a chat completion is asked of the face and through the gateway
acceptance.then: the face's usage is null and its rihmasto block says not measured, never zeros, and the gateway's audit records the tokens as not measured

acceptance.given: a capability whose declaration does not name the mcp face, and one that names it but is narrowed by RIHMA_FACES or --face
acceptance.when: MCP over stdio is asked to initialize and list its tools, with --face mcp, with --stdio alone and with no argument
acceptance.then: every request is answered with error -32001 and no tool is listed, while a capability that names the mcp face still answers over stdio

requirements.statement: A verified webhook or a relay event runs a small capability, a schedule runs it on its own, and its result goes out as a signed event the factory's own doorbell accepts.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: a capability started by a webhook whose secret is set
acceptance.when: deliveries arrive signed with Standard Webhooks (kernel/hooks.py), replayed, with a changed body, an old timestamp, another key, an oversized body, and to a capability whose secret is not set
acceptance.then: the verified delivery runs it once with the body as its input, a replay is answered 200 and not run, the others are refused (401, 413, 503) and run nothing

acceptance.given: a capability started by a rihma.signal.received event, subscribed to the relay by IT, with its results sent to a doorbell IT named
acceptance.when: a signal arrives and a relay round runs
acceptance.then: the relay's event runs it, an event of another type runs nothing, and its result goes out as a CloudEvent signed with Standard Webhooks that the factory accepts as one signal with the run's id as its ref, recorded as hook_received

acceptance.given: a scheduled capability served with its schedule on
acceptance.when: it is due, and when its guard does not pass
acceptance.then: it runs on its own when due, and while the guard holds every face it runs nothing

requirements.statement: rihmasto capability serve runs a delivered capability on this machine behind its pack guard and records the trace; capability check judges its declaration; the Compose file carries its faces.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: a delivered capability release
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability serve runs with --face mcp (stdio) and with --face openai --port 0, or with a face it does not offer, no port for an HTTP face, or a release it does not have
acceptance.then: it answers from the release with the pack's version, on 127.0.0.1 only, and the ledger records capability_served with the local user, the pack status that decided it, what was assumed and the pack and declaration hashes; a refusal exits 2 and writes nothing

acceptance.given: a delivered capability release
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability check runs
acceptance.then: it prints the declaration as the pack judges it, writes nothing, and a release it does not have exits 2

acceptance.given: a site's deploy package of a capability release
acceptance.when: its compose.yaml is rendered with the pack's runtime
acceptance.then: its one service carries RIHMA_FACES, the schedule when it is scheduled, every declared secret, the faces' token and the gateway's URL by name only, labels and header lines on how to reach each face; it validates and leaks nothing, and a web product's file is unchanged

acceptance.given: a shell that sets RIHMA_SCHEDULE=on and RIHMA_FACES
acceptance.when: rihmasto capability serve plans the faces process with and without --schedule
acceptance.then: the faces process inherits neither, and capability_served records whether the schedule runs: only with --schedule and a scheduled trigger

requirements.statement: Small capabilities are learnable and reachable (D-0017): the Releases tab shows a capability's runtime and faces, the assistant explains it and takes a person there, and the guide has a tutorial and says what is built and what is planned.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23: small things (a single workflow, an automation, an agentic capability) delivered where they must run, through MCP, an API or other integrations; D-0015 and D-0017.

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map and a project with a delivered capability
acceptance.when: a person asks the assistant how the capability is reached
acceptance.then: the map has the capability_faces control on the Releases tab, the answer takes the person to the project's Releases tab and that control, the page carries the control, and the guide has its tutorial and its built and planned lists

requirements.statement: An adopted system is assessed from every perspective: deterministic rules first, each finding with its evidence, severity and suggested change, and 'not measured' where the files cannot tell; the panel's model may propose more, kept apart; the assessment is a versioned record in the ledger, comparable over time and in the evidence pack; and a person turns chosen findings into change cards that go round the change loop.
requirements.notes: The owner's goal of 2026-11-23 for brownfield use: adopt an existing system, get multi-perspective fixes, develop it further. D-0014 (the red team is Rihmasto's own), D-0017 (the same trace on every path; every feature learnable and reachable).

acceptance.given: adopted good and poor fixture repositories (tests/fixtures/assess)
acceptance.when: each is assessed by rule
acceptance.then: the poor one fails rules in each of five perspectives (CI/CD governance, maintenance, security, compliance, architecture and operations), each finding with a severity, a suggested change and its evidence (a file and a line with the masked line, or a measured fact); the good one passes them; branch protection and required checks read 'not measured' with the reason, and nothing that could not be known reads passed

acceptance.given: an adopted repository with a filter, an eol attribute, a link and a credential planted at run time
acceptance.when: it is assessed
acceptance.then: the revision is read from git's objects (no filter runs, the bytes are the blob's, the link is not followed and is said); the red team's static findings are security findings with their rule, CWE and masked evidence; the credential reaches neither the record, the SARIF nor the ledger; what was not read leaves the scan's coverage not measured; and the SARIF beside the record is ingested by the security gate, which the next version counts

acceptance.given: a scripted model
acceptance.when: the intake panel's perspectives review the inventory and the rules' results
acceptance.then: each proposal is model_proposed, numbered apart (P-n), never counted with the rules' findings, with what it rests on checked (found, or not found in the repository); a malformed proposal is dropped and counted; a perspective whose call fails is not measured and the assessment is still recorded; the repository's text cannot close the data fence

acceptance.given: two assessments of a project
acceptance.when: they are recorded
acceptance.then: each is a version AS-n with its sha256 in the index and in the ledger's assessment_recorded record, with the D-0017 trace (who asked, decided by rule, delegated to whom, each assumed check with its reason, the revision and the SARIF's sha256); the second says what is new, resolved, still open and no longer measured, and any two compare; a record changed afterwards shows as not intact; no person, no repository or a bad ref is refused and records nothing

acceptance.given: an assessment
acceptance.when: a person files chosen findings (F-n and P-n)
acceptance.then: each becomes a change card signed by that person with origin 'assessment', triaged by rule as a new requirement that needs a business decision (or the class the person chose), its text naming the evidence, who found it and the suggested change; a finding whose card is still open is skipped; an unknown id, a non-person or an unknown class is refused; each card is assessment_change_opened in the ledger

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: rihmasto assess and rihmasto assessment list, show, compare and change run
acceptance.then: they assess, list every version with its sha256 checked, show one, compare two and file findings; a refusal exits 2 with the reason on stderr

acceptance.given: the cockpit's API
acceptance.when: a person assesses a project and files findings
acceptance.then: GET .../assessment reads; POST .../assessment assesses, signed by that person: by rule before it answers, with the panel through the cockpit's model in the background (409 without one; 400 without a repository; 403 for a non-person); POST .../assessment/changes files ticked findings as change cards; each write is also a cockpit_write

acceptance.given: an assessed project
acceptance.when: the MCP server and an evidence export read it
acceptance.then: rihma_assessment returns the latest or the named version and writes nothing; the evidence pack carries assessment.json with every version's sha256 checked, and a line in its README

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map and the guide
acceptance.when: a person asks Rihma where to assess a system
acceptance.then: the map's Assessment view and its two controls take the person there; docs/brownfield.md holds the guide, a tutorial and what is built and what is planned

acceptance.given: headless Chrome on the demo home
acceptance.when: a person opens the adopted project's Assessment tab
acceptance.then: they assess it, read its findings by perspective, tick one and file it as a change card, in dark and light, at 1440 and 390 px wide, with keyboard focus and accessible names, and with no console error, failed request or CSP violation

acceptance.given: an adopted system whose suite passed at adoption, and an upstream commit that adds a failing test
acceptance.when: main, the synced upstream and the adoption revision are assessed
acceptance.then: the characterisation baseline reads passed only at the adoption revision its suite ran at; at any other revision it is not measured, with a reason naming both revisions and the result at adoption, it is counted as not measured and listed among what was assumed

acceptance.given: a recorded assessment
acceptance.when: its record and its index entry are edited together so that they agree
acceptance.then: the record is still not intact, because it is checked against the sha256 in the ledger's hash-chained assessment_recorded record: the command line's list, the cockpit's view and the evidence pack (assessment.json and its README line) all say it changed since it was recorded

acceptance.given: a revision holding a file and a folder of the same name, and a credential on a dependency line a rule cites
acceptance.when: it is assessed
acceptance.then: the assessment is recorded and its notes say the file under the folder was not read; the rule's evidence names the file and line with the credential masked, and the credential reaches neither the record nor the ledger

acceptance.given: a package.json and a pyproject.toml that declare no dependency, and two perspectives of the panel that propose the same finding
acceptance.when: the system is assessed with a scripted model and both proposals are filed
acceptance.then: neither manifest is judged: the pinning check names only the requirements file as pinned; each proposal keeps a key naming its perspective, so both are filed as their own change cards and neither is skipped as already open

acceptance.given: a repository whose code reads a hard-coded dict with config.get, names 'audit' as a word and os.environ and an audit_log only in a comment, and whose README mentions privacy in passing; and one that reads os.environ, keeps an audit_log and has a 'Personal data' section
acceptance.when: each is assessed by rule
acceptance.then: the first fails 'configuration comes from the environment', reads the audit trail as not measured and fails 'how personal data is handled is written down'; the second passes all three with the line that shows each, and the personal-data pass says what the section says is not checked by rule

acceptance.given: a scripted model that records which model answered for one perspective of the panel only
acceptance.when: a project is assessed with it
acceptance.then: the record and its trace name that model for that perspective and 'not recorded' for every other

acceptance.given: a mirrored repository
acceptance.when: its revision is read, and a read fails
acceptance.then: the reader of the mirror's objects (git cat-file) has exited and its output is closed in both cases

acceptance.given: an assessed repository with open findings; the owner (2026-11-25): "in the assessment I should be able to ask Rihma what fixes to prioritise and why, and choose select all instead of clicking through each"
acceptance.when: a person asks Ask Rihma which findings to fix first, or opens the Assessment view
acceptance.then: by rule and with no model, the open findings not already filed as an open change come in order (severity, then security and compliance before the rest, then still open since the version before, the panel's opinions after the rules' findings), each with why; the answer takes the person to the assessment; the view offers select the top findings, critical and high, all open, and clear; each finding has its own suggested kind with why, which the person may change, and filing sends each ticked finding's own kind

requirements.statement: A project runs under a posture a person chose (prototype, balanced, production or regulated), tuned by priority weights from 0 to 3 for ux, security, compliance, speed and cost; every effect is a rule in the kernel, previewed before anyone chooses and recorded with who chose it.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: the four postures
acceptance.when: each is previewed (rihmasto posture preview, POST /api/postures/preview)
acceptance.then: prototype is assume mode at explore or demo with autonomy 3 and light gates; balanced is mixed at demo or pilot with autonomy 2 and standard gates; production runs at pilot or production with a security scan and the red team's static layer required, holdouts on staging, IT's deploy gate and an evidence pack; regulated is socratic at any maturity with autonomy 1, plan approval, confirmation by name, warnings blocking, the static and agentic layers and an attestable evidence pack; the same choice always gives the same preview, and a preview writes nothing

acceptance.given: a posture and priority weights
acceptance.when: they are previewed
acceptance.then: they set each perspective's question budget and emphasis, the spec's topics (accessibility for ux on work with screens, threat model for security, record-keeping and data protection for compliance), which findings block and the autonomy; a weight under the posture's floor is raised and the preview says so; an unknown weight or a value outside 0 to 3 is refused

acceptance.given: rihmasto new --posture, or a new project with a posture
acceptance.when: the project is made
acceptance.then: its mode and maturity are the posture's unless named; a maturity it does not run at or a looser mode is refused as a usage error and nothing is made; posture_chosen records the person, persona, weights and the preview they were shown; without a posture the project is made exactly as before

requirements.statement: The posture acts on the intake, the spec and the plan, by rule.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a project with a posture
acceptance.when: the panel reads its request
acceptance.then: each perspective's prompt carries its question budget and what it weighs, and no perspective files more questions than its budget

acceptance.given: a posture whose weights require topics

acceptance.given: a confirming posture (regulated, or compliance 3)
acceptance.when: it runs to the build
acceptance.then: every question is settled by a person before the spec, a person approves the plan at any maturity, approving confirms each requirement no named person confirmed in the approver's name (requirements_confirmed), and an open assumption holds the build until a person confirms or refutes it

requirements.statement: How much waits for a person follows the posture's autonomy, beneath the autonomy cap.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a posture whose autonomy is below a step's level

acceptance.given: a balanced project from an idea
acceptance.when: the pipeline runs it

requirements.statement: The posture decides which signals block a release.
requirements.notes: The owner chose presets plus weights (2026-11-23): a posture is one choice that sets how a project runs, changeable per project and during the run; every effect is a rule in the kernel (kernel/posture.py).

acceptance.given: a release past IT's deploy gate under a posture with evidence

acceptance.then: it waits until an evidence pack is exported for that release (attestable where the posture asks it), and a pack's security summary reports the findings alone

requirements.statement: A posture changed during the run says what it changes now and later, never silently.

acceptance.given: a project without a posture

requirements.statement: A person can use a very small part of Rihmasto or the whole of it, and change that later: a catalogue of modules with their dependencies and presets, chosen per factory and overridable per project

acceptance.then: each module says what it adds, what it needs and what it yields; enabling one enables what it needs and says so; turning off one another module needs, an unknown module or preset and an empty set are refused; every preset is closed under its needs and says what you bring and get
a factory where nobody chose is the full factory, and reading its set creates nothing; the full factory chosen by its preset still holds a module added to the catalogue later

a set is chosen by a named person with a persona that may choose, and recorded in the factory's ledger with from, to, preset, person, persona and reason; nothing is recorded when nothing changes; a project's own set and its return to the factory's are recorded in its ledger
`rihmasto modules show`, `modules presets` and `modules set` show and change the sets from the command line, refusing a writer who is not a person

requirements.notes: D-0017: every way of using Rihmasto, the full factory, spec only or gate my code among them, writes the same trace. The modules stream (docs/guides/use-only-what-you-need.md).
requirements.statement: What a set does: a module that is off is refused where it acts and hidden where it shows, and its records stay

acceptance.then: the command line refuses a command of a module that is off where it acts, with exit 2 and the command that turns it on, a project's own set taking precedence over the factory's; core commands always run

the pipeline stops at the edge of the set as done, saying why and what to do next, and records the stop once: spec only stops once the contract is compiled, a set without delivery stops before delivery

the cockpit refuses a write route of a module that is off with 403 and never a read; it reads and changes the factory's set and a project's own, signed and recorded; a project's views are only those of its modules that are on

the assistant's map, its model's catalogue and its navigation leave out what is off; asked about it, the assistant names the module that adds it and takes the person to Settings, Modules; with the assistant module off it answers from the map without a model

requirements.notes: D-0017: every way of using Rihmasto, the full factory, spec only or gate my code among them, writes the same trace. The modules stream (docs/guides/use-only-what-you-need.md).
requirements.statement: Each standalone preset works end to end from the command line with what exists today, and the person's own repository is never written

acceptance.then: spec only: a need becomes a confirmed spec and a hashed contract, exported with a report of who decided what and a manifest; nothing is built, holdout scenarios never leave their custody, the export is recorded and never replaces an earlier one

gate my code: a change in an attached repository meets the gate (tests, the trace, fail-first, the independent verifier, protected paths) in a temporary clone; the verdict is recorded with who asked and the revisions; without its verifier it is not measured; Rihmasto never merges

gate my code holdouts: scenarios are imported from a folder outside the repository (inside is refused), kept in custody, run against the person's running service, and the ledger keeps each criterion's verdict and never a scenario's steps

a repository is attached with a contract whose hash is checked, a spec file compiled with no model and endorsed by the person, or its own contract file; a URL, a folder that is not a repository and a changed contract are refused and leave nothing behind; the pipeline says what an attached repository waits for
security only: Rihmasto's own static scan of a committed revision of the repository feeds the security gate as SARIF, and a person accepts a finding's risk until a date

evidence only: the repository's releases (its tags) are recorded with the commit each names, git's claims marked as claims, and what the kernel saw at each; a moved tag is recorded again; the evidence pack carries them
assess only adopts and syncs an existing system, and capability only starts a project on the chain to a capability; each refuses, with how to turn it on, what its set does not hold

requirements.notes: D-0017: every way of using Rihmasto, the full factory, spec only or gate my code among them, writes the same trace. The modules stream (docs/guides/use-only-what-you-need.md).
requirements.statement: The cockpit shows only what is enabled, says what a module that is off would add, and lets a person choose the set: on a new home's first visit and in Settings

acceptance.then: the sidebar, the phone's bar, Home's widgets and key figures, the widget library, the palette, a project's views and the assistant's suggestions show only what is on; a page of a module that is off names the module and links to Settings, Modules, and so does the assistant
a new factory home offers a first-run choice of a preset, by keyboard, signed and recorded; Settings, Modules changes the factory's set and a project's own, and the page shows the change at once

these pages fit at 1440 and 390 pixels in the dark and the light theme with nothing spilling sideways, every control has an accessible name, and no step leaves a console error or a Content-Security-Policy violation

requirements.notes: D-0017: a module that is off is off on every surface, and turning one off never leaves a live thing that nobody may stop. The modules stream's repair (docs/guides/use-only-what-you-need.md).
requirements.statement: A module that is off is off on every surface: a website's chat, an inbound webhook, the MCP server's write tools and the assistant's proposals ask the same set; a safety switch is never refused; an attached repository's own tests run only where access lets outside code run

acceptance.given: a website chat made while Integrations was on, and a set where Integrations, or what the chat files into, is off
acceptance.when: the website sends a message, and an owner revokes the chat
acceptance.then: the chat takes no message and files nothing (the website is told the chat is turned off); revoking it is core on the command line and in the cockpit, signed and recorded, while creating one is refused; Settings still lists the chats made before, says Integrations is off and offers Revoke, by keyboard

acceptance.given: a set where the delivery square or the change loop is off where a write acts
acceptance.when: an MCP client calls rihma_signal or rihma_report_change
acceptance.then: the tool is refused with the module and the command that turns it on, nothing is written; a comment, which is core, is taken; every MCP tool that writes names the cockpit route whose module it asks

acceptance.given: a set where a module is off and the assistant's model is asked to act
acceptance.when: the model proposes an action, a route or a widget of that module
acceptance.then: the proposal is not offered: it is listed as dropped with the module's name and that Settings, Modules turns it on; with the module on where the project is, the same proposal is offered

acceptance.given: an attached repository and access enforced
acceptance.when: a person asks for repo gate or repo releases --check
acceptance.then: the repository's tests run only through IT's isolation runner, required before anything is cloned and serving this factory while they run; with no runner the request is refused (exit 2) and nothing runs; recording releases without checks runs no code and still works

acceptance.given: an inbound webhook source IT added while Integrations was on, and a set where Integrations, or what the source files into, is off
acceptance.when: a ring with a signature that holds arrives, and IT removes the source
acceptance.then: the ring is answered 403, this source is turned off, and nothing is stored (an unverified ring is still 401); removing a source, ending a subscription, disabling a connector and the lists they are found in are core on the command line, signed and recorded, while adding a source is refused (exit 2)

requirements.statement: Each audience's output is chosen by a named person, recorded and changeable, and built from the project's records and its release, the same records giving the same bytes.
requirements.notes: Outputs per audience, proposed by the outputs stream (kernel/outputs.py); vendor-proposed until the owner confirms it. docs/guides/outputs.md marks what is built and what is planned.

acceptance.given: a project with no choice yet
acceptance.when: a person chooses its outputs, and chooses again
acceptance.then: outputs.json and an outputs_chosen ledger record keep who chose, as which persona, why, and what was chosen before, added and removed, with the history; a persona outside the choosers, a name that is not a person or an unknown target is refused and records nothing; before any choice the work profile's proposal is shown as proposed, never as chosen

acceptance.given: chosen and unchosen targets
acceptance.when: a person builds outputs
acceptance.then: a target nobody chose, or a builder outside the builders' personas, is refused and nothing is recorded; every build, made or not, is an output_built record with the person and persona; a target that cannot be built yet says why in plain words (the MCP server is planned)

acceptance.given: the same records and release
acceptance.when: the report, API, container and source are built twice, by two people
acceptance.then: each zip has the same name (its content's sha256) and the same bytes; every entry carries a fixed time; MANIFEST.json holds the sha256 of every file

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: rihmasto output <pid> runs with no flag, --choose and --target
acceptance.then: it shows the targets, chooses and builds; a choice or a build without --person and --persona is refused with exit 2

requirements.statement: A product chosen to be a web app people sign in to gets the paved road's sign-in, checked at every gate and owned by the road.
requirements.notes: Outputs per audience, proposed by the outputs stream (kernel/outputs.py); vendor-proposed until the owner confirms it. docs/guides/outputs.md marks what is built and what is planned.

acceptance.given: the template with the road's sign-in
acceptance.when: its own suite runs, and runs again with the sign-in removed or weakened
acceptance.then: the suite passes, the road's sign-in checks among them (salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes of at least 600000 rounds, an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie that is Secure over TLS, a CSRF token on every state-changing request, a lockout after repeated failures, the first admin from the environment, the proxy mode for the organisation's own sign-in); without the sign-in, or with a cheap hash, no CSRF check, no lockout or a cookie scripts can read, it fails

acceptance.given: a product with sign-in
acceptance.when: the red team's static rules scan it
acceptance.then: they find nothing; the Dockerfile runs the service as an unprivileged user that owns /data; the operator's guide names the first admin's and the proxy's settings

acceptance.given: a person chooses the web app with sign-in
acceptance.when: before the product's repository exists, and after it
acceptance.then: the repository starts with the sign-in; an existing product gains it on main only when its whole suite passes with it (sign_in_added), a server without the sign-in hook is refused and main does not move (sign_in_refused), the choice is then not recorded; no builder cell may change app/sign_in.py or its tests

acceptance.given: the product's server
acceptance.when: a request reaches it
acceptance.then: every request goes through the guards before its handler, an unknown path and a wrong method included; handle() runs a handler without them for the product's tests; a repeated header reaches a guard as all its values; a sign-in request's body never reaches the traffic log

acceptance.given: the template with the road's sign-in
acceptance.when: its sign-in is changed to keep a session token that arrived with the sign-in request
acceptance.then: the road's own checks fail (session fixation is caught at every gate); the road's sign-in issues a fresh token, and a planted token, made up or someone else's live session, never signs the person in

acceptance.given: a product compiled without sign-in
acceptance.when: a person chooses the web app with sign-in later
acceptance.then: main's Dockerfile runs the service as the unprivileged user that owns /data and the red team's static rules find nothing; the sign_in_added record and factory/SIGN-IN.md say how a data volume made before is handed over once

requirements.statement: A developer, an integrator and a team each get their output: a container, an API description and the source.
requirements.notes: Outputs per audience, proposed by the outputs stream (kernel/outputs.py); vendor-proposed until the owner confirms it. docs/guides/outputs.md marks what is built and what is planned.

acceptance.given: a release
acceptance.when: the container output is built
acceptance.then: it holds the product's source as committed at the release revision with its Dockerfile, a compose.yaml that publishes the service on 127.0.0.1:8080 with its data on a named volume, image.json and a README on how to run it; with sign-in, compose takes the first admin from the shell, never with a value

acceptance.given: a release
acceptance.when: the API output is built
acceptance.then: it is an OpenAPI 3.1 document with every route of the spec's interface and /health; each operation lists the criteria whose action names it, with their evidence state, and the status codes they expect; with sign-in, the sign-in routes are open and every other operation needs the session cookie and the CSRF header

acceptance.given: a release
acceptance.when: the source output is built
acceptance.then: it is a git bundle that git bundle verify accepts and that clones to a history holding the release's revision, with the commands to put it on a branch of the team's own; Rihmasto pushes nothing

acceptance.given: the source output, with a release and without one
acceptance.when: its README's commands run, word for word, in a folder outside any repository
acceptance.then: every command succeeds: the clone checks main out, the bundle verifies inside it, and the team's repository receives a branch at the release's revision, or at main's tip when there is no release

requirements.statement: A business owner gets a plain delivery report, in HTML and Markdown, every statement traceable to a record.
requirements.notes: Outputs per audience, proposed by the outputs stream (kernel/outputs.py); vendor-proposed until the owner confirms it. docs/guides/outputs.md marks what is built and what is planned.

acceptance.given: a project with a release, a decision and assumptions
acceptance.when: its report is written
acceptance.then: it has the eight sections (what was asked and by whom, what was built, the decisions, the assumptions, the evidence, how to try it, the cost, the limits); each statement names the record it rests on; who asked, who decided as which persona, each assumption's state and each criterion's evidence are said in words; an unpriced cost reads not measured, never 0

acceptance.given: outputs built since
acceptance.when: the report is written again
acceptance.then: it is the same; the HTML escapes every value, runs no script and loads nothing from outside

requirements.statement: The cockpit's Outputs view: pick the targets, build them, download them, with what each contains.
requirements.notes: Outputs per audience, proposed by the outputs stream (kernel/outputs.py); vendor-proposed until the owner confirms it. docs/guides/outputs.md marks what is built and what is planned.

acceptance.given: the cockpit
acceptance.when: the outputs API is called
acceptance.then: GET shows the seven targets with what each holds; PUT chooses, signed, and a persona that may not is a 403; POST .../outputs/build builds and hands each file over through a link that works once; a target not chosen is a 403; a new project's request may name its outputs, chosen at intake by the requester, and is refused before the project is made when the persona may not choose

acceptance.given: a demo home in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person asks the assistant for the outputs and uses the Outputs view
acceptance.then: the assistant takes them there; they choose by keyboard, build and download, in the dark and the light theme at 1440 and 390 px wide, every control named, nothing wider than the screen, with no console error, failed request or CSP violation; skipped when Chrome is not installed

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map

requirements.statement: An MCP server output plugs into the small-capability faces, and a posture may propose outputs, each through a documented hook.

acceptance.given: no faces module, or one without output_files
acceptance.when: the MCP server target is shown and built

acceptance.given: a postures module that offers proposed_outputs, or none
acceptance.when: a project's outputs are shown before anyone chose
acceptance.then: the posture's proposal is shown as proposed, never as chosen, and nothing is recorded; a proposal naming an unknown target, or no hook, falls back to the work profile's proposal

requirements.statement: What a chosen output settles is known everywhere it matters: the factory's own checks never count the sign-in turning them away as a product failure, intake never asks it again, and the builder is told how the sign-in works.

acceptance.given: a running product with the road's sign-in
acceptance.when: the holdout runner, a probe round and a shadow replay send requests without a session
acceptance.then: a step the sign-in turns away that expected no 401 is not measured, never failed; a step that expects the 401 passes and a real mismatch still fails; the probe round counts it as neither a check nor a failure; a shadow replay that met the sign-in is not measured, never passed, and the canary leaves those requests out of its sample

acceptance.given: a project whose web app with sign-in was chosen at intake
acceptance.when: the intake panel runs
acceptance.then: the panel's prompt names what the choice settles, a question on sign-in or single sign-on is not asked and a question_not_asked record names it with the person who chose; the brief, which the spec reads, keeps the choice as that person's word; a project without the choice is still asked

acceptance.given: a product with the road's sign-in, and one without
acceptance.when: a builder's envelope is written

requirements.notes: D-0017 (governance everywhere: autopilot in a sandbox is one of the paths, and no path skips the record) and D-0007 (delegated conclusions); the owner asked for both ends: let Rihmasto run on its own in a test sandbox, or keep a tight hold, and see whether a project stays on track.
requirements.statement: A person whose persona may decide a kind of card delegates named card kinds on one project, for at most seven days, to one of the factory's deterministic rules; the pipeline decides those cards by the rule in that person's name and persona, and nothing outside the delegation is decided.

acceptance.given: a delegation of questions (rule assume) by a person as a persona
acceptance.when: the pipeline waits on a blocking question
acceptance.then: it assumes the question with the asking perspective's proposal and goes on; the decision records the delegating person, the persona and the delegation id on the decision record, the card's copy and the ledger; a decision with a reason of its own says 'by delegation DL-n (rule)'; a delegated_decision record keeps the rule and its basis

acceptance.given: delegations of the plan's approval (plan_when_tested) and of escalations (retry_once)
acceptance.when: the plan or an escalation waits
acceptance.then: a plan whose every requirement has a test, every criterion a check, that compiles and contradicts no paved road is approved, and the pipeline's own plan gate sees it approved; a plan with a requirement with no test, and an approval that is not the plan's, wait for a person, the reason in the ledger once; an escalated task is retried once, and when it escalates again the card waits for a person; the rule never accepts as is and never stops a build

acceptance.given: a delegation
acceptance.when: it is revoked, or its time passes, or a card of a kind not delegated waits
acceptance.then: the next card of that kind waits for a person at once; a card of a kind not delegated is never decided; only the delegator or a persona that decides a delegated kind may revoke; a delegation longer than seven days, ending in the past, with an unreadable time or naming no person is refused

acceptance.given: a request to delegate
acceptance.when: it names deploy_gate, trust, holdout_ruling, connector, road, concept, a kind with no rule, a kind the persona may not decide, or an unknown rule
acceptance.then: it is refused with the reason and nothing is recorded

acceptance.given: access enforced (D-0016)
acceptance.when: a verified identity delegates and the delegation later decides
acceptance.then: only a verified identity granted the persona may delegate; the delegated decision names that identity and the delegation, and is checked again against the access file, so a grant IT removed refuses it and the card waits, with the refusal in the ledger

requirements.notes: D-0017 (governance everywhere: autopilot in a sandbox is one of the paths, and no path skips the record) and D-0007 (delegated conclusions); the owner asked for both ends: let Rihmasto run on its own in a test sandbox, or keep a tight hold, and see whether a project stays on track.
requirements.statement: An autopilot run delegates named card kinds until a time and runs the pipeline on its own, bound to a sandbox: it delivers only to the local preview or a road marked sandbox, sends events only to sandbox receivers, keeps connectors read-only, and a person stops it.

acceptance.given: rihmasto autopilot start <pid> --until --delegate --person --persona (or the cockpit)
acceptance.when: the project lands on the local preview
acceptance.then: the run delegates the kinds in the starter's name, runs pass after pass until a person is needed or it is done, and records autopilot_started, each pass and each delegated decision in the ledger; autopilot status shows the run, its sandbox, its delegation and what it decided

acceptance.given: a run on a project that lands in staging, or on a demo road not marked sandbox
acceptance.when: the pipeline would deliver
acceptance.then: it waits for a person with the reason, nothing is deployed and no road card is opened, and the hold is in the ledger once; a demo road IT marked "sandbox": true is delivered to; staging and production are never a sandbox

acceptance.given: a run that holds a project
acceptance.when: the relay runs, or a connector would write
acceptance.then: a subscription IT has not marked as a sandbox receiver gets none of the project's events: they wait in order, the hold is logged once, and they go after a person stops the run; a sandbox receiver gets them; only IT marks a receiver; write_hold answers that a connector write waits for a person

acceptance.given: a run
acceptance.when: a person stops it, or its time passes, or a second run is started
acceptance.then: stopping revokes its delegation at once and the next card waits; once its time passes no pass runs and the sandbox holds until a person stops it; one run holds a project at a time; a persona that may not pause may not start or stop one; posture_preset offers the 'autopilot sandbox' preset

acceptance.given: the cockpit
acceptance.when: a person starts or stops an autopilot, or revokes a delegation, from a project's Track view
acceptance.then: each write is signed with the person and persona through the kernel, which refuses what it does not allow; in headless Chrome, dark at 1440 px and light at 390 px, the Home widget, the Track pill and the Track view work with the keyboard focus kept, every control named, and no console error, failed request, CSP violation or sideways scroll

requirements.notes: D-0017 (governance everywhere: autopilot in a sandbox is one of the paths, and no path skips the record) and D-0007 (delegated conclusions); the owner asked for both ends: let Rihmasto run on its own in a test sandbox, or keep a tight hold, and see whether a project stays on track.
requirements.statement: Track says, deterministically and with every figure's basis, how a project is doing against its approved plan: on track, at risk, off track or not measured, with reasons; human checkpoints show when a person must look and can hold the run.

acceptance.given: a project
acceptance.when: track runs
acceptance.then: each figure (baseline, tasks, gate first round and its trend, assumption debt, scope changes, cards holding the run and their age, time and cost against the budget, posture) has its value and basis, and a figure with nothing to rest on is not measured with the reason, never zero or passed; with no approved plan and nothing wrong the answer is not_measured

acceptance.given: records that put a project at risk or off track
acceptance.when: an escalation is open, a card waits 3 or 7 days, an assumption is past due, first-round passes fall, changes pile up, the due date passes, spend exceeds the budget or the posture hook says not kept
acceptance.then: the answer is at_risk or off_track with each reason naming its figure, and the same records give the same answer

acceptance.given: checkpoints a plan owner set on a project
acceptance.when: the project reaches a checkpoint's stage
acceptance.then: the checkpoint is due until a person records a look; with hold the pipeline waits at it, on record once, and goes on after the look; a look at a stage not reached, or checkpoints set by another persona, are refused

acceptance.given: a project
acceptance.when: a person reads it from the command line, the cockpit or the MCP server
acceptance.then: rihmasto track, GET /api/projects/<pid>/track, the project's Track pill, the dashboard's track read model and the MCP reads rihma_track and rihma_autopilot show the same track, and reading writes nothing

acceptance.given: a relay notice subscription IT set to a daily digest
acceptance.when: the relay runs
acceptance.then: it sends one digest a UTC day through the notice sink with every project's answer, defanged titles and one link, to the cockpit's Home; a failed digest is tried again next round and every attempt is logged; a webhook subscription cannot take a digest

requirements.notes: An independent check of the autopilot stream (D-0017, D-0007): a pass a person stopped still delivered outside the sandbox, the daily digest named a held project to receivers outside the sandbox, and the project header showed two on-track answers that could disagree.
requirements.statement: An autopilot's sandbox holds to the end: a pass it started never leaves the sandbox even after a person stops the run, the daily digest leaves its project out for receivers outside the sandbox, and a project shows one on-track answer.

acceptance.given: an autopilot pass under way on a project whose landing road is not marked sandbox
acceptance.when: a person stops the autopilot while the pass runs (the command line, or the cockpit's Stop)
acceptance.then: the pass delivers nothing and writes through no connector, ends at its next safe point (between pipeline steps or tasks) in state stopped with the stop on record once, the cockpit's Stop says the autopilot job ends there, and only a pass a person runs afterwards delivers

acceptance.given: a notice subscription that asks for the daily Track digest and an autopilot that holds a project
acceptance.when: the relay sends the digest
acceptance.then: a subscription IT has not marked as a sandbox receiver gets a digest without that project's title or reasons, only how many projects were left out; a sandbox receiver gets it listed; the relay's record names the projects held

acceptance.given: a project with a track
acceptance.when: a person opens it in the cockpit, or reads its track
acceptance.then: the project header shows one on-track answer (the Track pill, never beside a health chip with the same words) and the Health card shows that same answer; the track carries every reason the health reads, so an approval gone stale or a last release that stopped makes it at risk

requirements.statement: Any input, from any author, is read for what it is: what it states is kept as given with its lines and never asked again, the facet checklist finds the gaps and the mode settles them, and the intake summary shows from your input, asked and assumed side by side.
requirements.notes: D-0017: every path writes the same trace (who asked, what was given, what was assumed, what proves it), and the feature is learnable and reachable (docs/guides/inputs.md, cockpit/ui_map.json). Kernel: kernel/input_kind.py, kernel/input_facets.py, kernel/input_intake.py, kernel/input_summary.py.

acceptance.given: a one-line need, a two-line Finnish need, an expert's specification with ids and criteria, a full plan with three deliberate gaps, and a folder of mixed documents (tests/fixtures/inputs)
acceptance.when: each is read by rule
acceptance.then: each is read as its kind (need, need, specification, plan, folder) with its language and the rules that decided it; a folder's documents are each read as their own kind; a long text with no structure is a need, read as uncertain

acceptance.given: the same inputs
acceptance.when: the facet checklist reads them
acceptance.then: every fact the input states is kept with its facet, document and lines, quoting the author's own words; the gaps are exactly the facets it does not state (all thirteen for the one-line need; data and its sensitivity, availability and acceptance criteria for the plan); the author's requirements keep their ids, statements and given / when / then criteria, and a plan's decisions their lines; a section that says only TBD leaves its facet open, with its lines

acceptance.given: an intake whose panel asks again what the input states
acceptance.when: the panel's questions are screened
acceptance.then: a question every facet of which the input states is not asked, and is recorded with the facts it rests on, in the reading and the ledger; the panel is told, word for word in one shared prefix, what the input states and what its gaps are; for a need, the profile's standing questions are still asked

acceptance.given: a specification, a plan or a folder in socratic, assume or mixed mode
acceptance.when: intake runs
acceptance.then: the checklist asks its own question for each gap no question covers, from the maturity that needs it (and as a posture preset changes that); socratic puts every asked question to a person, assume assumes each with a due date, mixed sends the blocking gaps (users and roles, outcomes, scope, data) to a person and assumes the rest; a need's gaps are the panel's to ask, so the checklist adds none

acceptance.given: an expert's specification and a plan
acceptance.when: the spec is written from the analyst's draft, and the plan is taken in
acceptance.then: each of the author's requirements keeps its id, its statement and its criteria word for word, with the draft's criterion kinds by place, as customer-endorsed by whoever asked; one the draft left out is kept as written and marked restored; the contract compiles from them; a plan's decisions arrive as given in the brief, never as an assumption, a question or a decision in the canon

acceptance.given: a recorded reading
acceptance.when: a named person asks the analyst's model to refine it
acceptance.then: the model's proposal is kept as model_proposed beside the rule's reading, with only the facets and lines the kernel checked and quoted itself, and what it left out with why; it changes no kind, question or decision; a model is never the one who asks; when no model answers it is not measured and nothing is written; in a folder a cited line is placed in its own document

acceptance.given: a project whose input was read
acceptance.when: a person asks for the intake summary on the command line or through the cockpit's API
acceptance.then: the summary sets from your input (facts, decisions, requirements with their lines), asked (with the answer and who gave it) and assumed (with the assumption and its due date) side by side, beside the questions not asked and every facet's state; `rihmasto inputs summary` prints it as JSON or text and `rihmasto inputs read` reads a request without writing; the ledger records who asked, the kind, every fact with its lines and the request's sha256, and the screening

acceptance.given: the cockpit on a project whose plan was taken in
acceptance.when: a person opens its Questions view in Chrome
acceptance.then: the intake summary shows its three columns side by side at 1440 px and stacked at 390 px with no sideways scroll, in light and dark; its regions are named by their headings; Tab reaches its first link and Enter opens that question; the facet checklist opens from the keyboard; Ask Rihma's Take me there brings the person to it; and no console error or CSP violation occurs

requirements.statement: Screening never drops a question that asks more than the input states, a blocking question always reaches the mode, and a folder's housekeeping files are never read as the author's request.
requirements.notes: Repair of FR-IK1 after an independent check (docs/guides/inputs.md, Never asked again). Kernel: kernel/input_intake.py (already_given, new_words), kernel/intake.py (folder_files, HOUSEKEEPING).

acceptance.given: an expert's specification that states its users, outcomes, performance and acceptance, and a panel whose questions name those facets
acceptance.when: the panel's questions are screened
acceptance.then: a question with any word of its own that the stated facts of its facets and the input's titles do not hold (deleting a tool, an email reminder, working offline, the tests before a release) is asked; only a question that restates is not asked; a blocking question that restates is still asked, so the mode can put it to a person, with its rationale citing the facts and their lines, and the reading and the ledger record it as restated

acceptance.given: a folder with a README, a notes file and docs/design.md beside CHANGELOG, LICENSE, SECURITY, CONTRIBUTING and requirements.txt files
acceptance.when: intake reads the folder
acceptance.then: the request holds the README, the notes and the design only; a housekeeping file states no facet, so a security policy does not mark security as given and a sign-in question is not screened away

requirements.statement: Rihmasto scans whatever a project folder holds instead of expecting certain files: every file is read, summarised, listed or skipped with its reason, secrets are never read, the person sees what would leave before anything is sent to a model, confidential material stays on local models, and an existing project may be any folder.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "rihmasto should be smart enough to just scan what's going on with the given project instead of expecting strictly certain files"; whatever is read is sent to the configured model endpoint, which may be a hosted provider, so the person must see what leaves before it leaves. Kernel: kernel/material.py, kernel/material_read.py, kernel/material_kinds.py, kernel/material_cli.py, kernel/material_adopt.py, kernel/confidential.py, kernel/source_guard.py; cockpit/static/scan.js. Docs: docs/guides/inputs.md, docs/brownfield.md. FR-MAT1-AC-10 was decided by the owner on 2026-11-24 after a journey test walked their real flows ("1. Yes 2. Skip 3. Agreed 4. Ask"): it is "2. Skip".

acceptance.given: a real project folder of Markdown, text, HTML, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument text, slides and sheet, CSV, JSON, YAML, PDF, a deploy log, pictures and code (tests/material_fixture.py)
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: each format's text is taken by rule with no model: headings kept, scripts and styles dropped and entities decoded, slides in the deck's own order with their numbers, each sheet's name, header and first rows, a structured file's keys, a log's first and last lines, a PDF's Flate text said to be partly read and a scanned PDF not read: no text layer; each file is classified as brief or spec, plan, review, handover, notes, log, data, slides, code or other; code becomes an inventory of languages, entry points, test folders, dependency manifests and CI workflows and is never read as text; the same folder scans the same way every time

acceptance.given: the folder also holds an environment file, an SSH key, a credentials file, a note whose text holds a token and code holding a cloud key
acceptance.when: it is scanned and its request is built
acceptance.then: each is listed as skipped: may hold secrets (never opened by its name, or its text holds a credential), and no secret appears in the request, the material map, the ledger, the panel's prompts, a snapshot or the cockpit page

acceptance.given: a folder whose documents are larger than the budget, and exclusions by path, glob and folder
acceptance.when: it is scanned
acceptance.then: the most telling files are read first (the README, briefs and specs, then plans, reviews, handovers and the code inventory, then notes and slides, then data and logs), a long one is summarised to its first part and the rest are listed, every cut is named in the map's cut notes with why, the request never exceeds the budget, dependency, build, cache, virtual environment and version-control folders are not walked, and the person's exclusions are skipped with the pattern that dropped them

acceptance.given: a folder given as intake's source
acceptance.when: intake runs
acceptance.then: the request is built from the material map, each part headed with its file path and kind; the map is kept in the project (material.json) and the ledger records its counts, never a file's contents; the any-input reading reads each part as its own document; a request confirmed from a scan arrives as text and keeps its documents by the map's digest

acceptance.given: a person at the command line
acceptance.when: they run rihmasto scan on a folder, and rihmasto new with that folder as the source
acceptance.then: scan prints what would be read, summarised, listed and skipped and why, the characters it comes to and where they would go; new shows the same map and creates nothing and sends nothing without --yes or a yes at the terminal; with it the map is recorded with the person and how they confirmed, and --exclude drops files

acceptance.given: the cockpit's New project dialog
acceptance.when: a person asks for a folder's preview, or creates or adopts a project from a scanned folder
acceptance.then: POST /api/source/preview answers a named person with a persona that may create or adopt a project, only for a folder under the home or a configured root, never a system folder or a folder of keys, and records nothing; the files the person unticked travel with the create and adopt requests, a created project keeps the map the person saw with who confirmed it, and its request leaves the unticked files out

acceptance.given: a project marked confidential: keep on local models, and a role routed to a hosted endpoint
acceptance.when: intake, the spec, the holdouts, a build, a change's triage, a refinement or a run would call a model for it
acceptance.then: the call is refused before anything is sent, with the role and its endpoint named and how to configure a local model (docs/guides/local-models.md), the refusal is recorded, a run stops in a refused state and the cockpit and the command line refuse before a project is created; the setting is recorded in the ledger; with every role on loopback or a private address the work goes on

acceptance.given: An existing project given as a git repository, a folder with code that is not a git repository, or a folder of documents only
acceptance.when: it is adopted
acceptance.then: a git repository is adopted as before and its documents are scanned as context; a folder that is not one is snapshotted into a new git repository under the factory home with only the files that pass the scan's rules, committed as the baseline and adopted from there, and the person's folder is never changed; a folder with no code is refused with the offer to start a new project from it as material

acceptance.given: a person in the cockpit in a real browser, light and dark, 1440 and 390 px wide
acceptance.when: they give New project a folder, scan it, untick a file and adopt it, and give it a folder of documents only
acceptance.then: the scan step shows the map grouped by read, summarised, unticked, listed and skipped with each reason, unticking scans again without the file and keeps the focus on it, adopt starts the job with the exclusion, a documents-only folder is offered as material for a new project and created from it; no secret is on the page, nothing scrolls sideways, and there is no console error, failed request or CSP violation

acceptance.given: a confidential project whose role's primary endpoint is local and whose fallback is hosted, and one whose primary is hosted
acceptance.when: the project's intake, spec, holdouts, build, refinement, change or assistant asks that role
acceptance.then: the local role is not refused: the hosted fallback is skipped and never called, because the lanes the project's calls run in (the analyst lane, the assistant's, the product surface and an adopted project's) are compiled without it, so no request reaches a hosted endpoint even when the local one fails; the ledger records confidential_fallback_skipped once per run, naming the role and the host; a role whose primary endpoint is hosted is refused as before

requirements.statement: A person publishes a version by pushing its tag: the suite and the contract run again, the source archives, an SBOM, checksums and the notes are built from the tagged commit, and a GitHub Release publishes them with a signed build provenance attestation; nothing is published from a tag that does not match the declared version.
requirements.notes: The owner asked that the CI/CD pipeline work, and approved a release workflow on 2026-11-24 ("Yes do"). Rihmasto runs from a checkout, so the source archive is the release; no wheel and no image. tools/release_build.py, .github/workflows/release.yml, docs/maintainers.md.

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares 1.2.0
acceptance.when: a release is built for a tag that is not v1.2.0, is not a version, or for a version the changelog has no section for
acceptance.then: the build is refused with the reason and no file is written

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares 1.2.0 and whose changelog has a [1.2.0] section
acceptance.when: a release is built for the tag v1.2.0
acceptance.then: it holds a .tar.gz and a .zip of the files git tracks at HEAD under rihmasto-1.2.0/, a CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM naming rihmasto 1.2.0, its licence, the archives' hashes and Gnomon as its one runtime dependency, SHA256SUMS that verify, and the notes word for word from the [1.2.0] section; building again from the same commit gives the same bytes

acceptance.given: a declared version that is an alpha, beta, release candidate or development version
acceptance.when: a rehearsal is built, or a release for it
acceptance.then: the rehearsal takes the declared version and the [Unreleased] notes, and the release is marked a pre-release

acceptance.given: the release workflow
acceptance.when: a person pushes a version tag, or runs the workflow by hand
acceptance.then: the suite and the contract run before anything is built; the provenance attestation and the GitHub Release happen only for a pushed tag; the workflow reads by default, only the publishing job may write contents, no expression is expanded inside a script, and a run by hand publishes nothing

acceptance.given: the checkout's package directories (each with an __init__.py under kernel, adapters, cockpit, embed and mcp)
acceptance.when: pyproject.toml's packages are read
acceptance.then: they list every one of them, kernel.checks, kernel.insights, kernel.redteam and kernel.runners included, and nothing else

requirements.statement: The acceptance matrix the owner tests against is written down and kept true to its tests.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: docs/acceptance.md and the tests in tests/acceptance
acceptance.when: the matrix is checked
acceptance.then: every row (G1 to G4, B, W, A, C1, C2, I) and column (socratic, assume, mixed; explore, demo, pilot, production; prototype, balanced, production and regulated postures; single operator and enforced access) has a cell, and every row but B a production cell; each cell's state is passes, fails or pending; a passing cell names offline tests that exist and are not expected failures; a failing cell names its test marked as an expected failure; a pending cell says why; every acceptance test is named by a cell

acceptance.given: the mode sweep's measured counts on docs/acceptance.md
acceptance.when: each need of the sweep is filed in mixed mode at demo
acceptance.then: each need's number of questions and of blocking questions is the one the page states

acceptance.given: the matrix's requirements in contract/contract.json
acceptance.when: their provenance is read
acceptance.then: each is vendor-proposed, the stream's own wording, and none claims the owner decided it

requirements.statement: A need from one line, two vague lines, a written spec or another language is asked, specified, built through the gate and delivered, offline.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: the one-line need 'We need room booking for the office.' in mixed mode at demo maturity
acceptance.when: intake and the run go, and Aino answers the blocking questions and accepts the demo
acceptance.then: exactly the two blocking questions are cards, the rest assumed; no spec is written before the answers; each requirement's provenance follows its source (endorsed, confirmed by Aino, or proposed); every task merges through the gate; the holdout passes on the demo's twin from its custody; the pack is valid

acceptance.given: the two-line vague need about customer service email, mixed, demo
acceptance.when: the run goes and Aino answers the three blocking questions and accepts the demo
acceptance.then: nothing is built before the answers; the AI requirement rests on Aino's answer; sending without a person is out of scope; the pack is valid

acceptance.given: a written spec handed in as a markdown file with ids VIS-001 to VIS-004
acceptance.when: the run goes in mixed mode at demo and Aino accepts the demo
acceptance.then: the facet checklist asks the one blocking facet the spec leaves out (what data it holds and how sensitive it is) as the only card and assumes the rest; no spec is written before it is answered; the spec keeps the author's ids VIS-001 to VIS-004 and adds the retention rule as an assumption; every task passes the gate; the holdout passes; the pack is valid

acceptance.given: a need in Finnish, mixed, explore
acceptance.when: the run goes after Aino answers the blocking question
acceptance.then: the profile is clear; the request, the questions and the spec stay in Finnish; the release lands on the preview with nobody after the answer; the pack is valid

requirements.statement: Each mode puts to a person exactly what it says, for every need, and both ends of the mode scale run end to end.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: each of the nine needs of the greenfield and small-thing rows
acceptance.when: intake runs in socratic, assume and mixed mode and the run takes one step
acceptance.then: socratic makes every question a card and assumes nothing; assume assumes every question with a proposal and puts only the unproposed profile question to a person; mixed puts exactly the blocking ones to a person; each assumption has a due date; no spec is written while a blocking question is open

acceptance.given: the one-line need in socratic mode at demo
acceptance.when: Aino lets the factory assume one card, answers every other and accepts the demo
acceptance.then: every question was a card; the run waited for the blocking ones; every requirement resting on a question is customer-confirmed by Aino; the one assumption names her as its chooser

acceptance.given: the one-line need in assume mode at demo
acceptance.when: the run goes and Aino accepts the demo
acceptance.then: no question card; the requirements resting on questions are assumptions due in 14 days; the acceptance is the only decision

requirements.statement: Every use case lands where its maturity says, after exactly the people the maturity names, up to production.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: the one-line need at explore, pilot and production
acceptance.when: the run goes and each card's owner says yes
acceptance.then: explore lands on the preview with nobody and records the dropped requirement; pilot waits for the plan approval and the user validation and lands on staging; production adds IT's deploy gate, a candidate and a canary that promotes, at stage 7; each release's steps are its maturity's plan

acceptance.given: each greenfield and small-thing row at production maturity
acceptance.when: the run goes and the business owner approves the plan and accepts the validation and IT approves the deploy gate
acceptance.then: the release is promoted to production by the canary, the plan approval is recorded, the deploy gate is decided by IT, and the pack is valid

requirements.statement: An existing service is adopted, assessed and developed further through the gate, and the gaps on the way to delivery are measured.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells. Its expected-failure criteria propose behaviour the owner has not decided; they record a gap measured today, not a promise.

acceptance.given: the stock levels repository with its own three unittest tests
acceptance.when: Olli adopts it, scans it with Rihmasto's own static layer, Pekka files the low-stock change, Aino accepts it and Olli applies it
acceptance.then: the baseline is 3 of 3 passed; the as-is spec is observed; the security gate goes from not measured to passed; the change is triaged as a new requirement needing a decision; T-002 merges with tests, trace and fail-first passed

acceptance.given: the adopted service with the change merged
acceptance.when: the run goes
acceptance.then: the developed service lands on the preview road (expected failure today: no paved road runs an adopted repository)

acceptance.given: an accepted change card on the adopted service
acceptance.when: the run goes, as the cockpit's Advance starts it
acceptance.then: the run carries out the accepted change (expected failure today: only rihmasto apply does, and the cockpit has no step for it)

acceptance.given: a repository whose unittest suite sits at its root beside its module, with no tests/ folder and no pytest marker
acceptance.when: Olli adopts it to improve it, and the gate's test signal is read on it
acceptance.then: the baseline runs the suite by unittest discovery from the root and measures it (2 of 2 passed); the gate, which discovers only under tests/, says not measured with no test run; docs/acceptance.md says both of the schedule candidate

requirements.statement: Small things (a workflow, an automation, an assistant, an ops agent, an integration) are delivered with their capability pack.
requirements.notes: Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: the purchase approval workflow, mixed, explore
acceptance.when: Aino answers the blocking question and the run goes
acceptance.then: it is proposed as an agentic workflow, its own question is assumed, it lands on the preview, and the pack is a capability pack that says its holdout was not measured

acceptance.given: the monthly invoice summary, assume, explore
acceptance.when: the run goes with no person
acceptance.then: the profile is a guess and says so; nothing goes to a person; every answer is an assumption on record; no requirement is customer-confirmed; it lands on the preview

acceptance.given: the travel policy assistant, mixed, demo
acceptance.when: the run goes and Aino answers which kind of work it is and accepts the demo
acceptance.then: the profile question waits in every mode; the answer chooses the profile in Aino's name; the spec holds a refusal; the holdout passes; the pack is a capability pack

acceptance.given: the access review ops agent, assume, demo
acceptance.when: the run goes and Aino accepts the demo
acceptance.then: the ops agent's own questions are assumed; its holdout passes against the demo; the pack is a report

acceptance.given: the shipment webhook integration, assume, explore
acceptance.when: the demo's own webhook cell builds it
acceptance.then: its questions are assumed and the dead-letter requirement rests on one as an assumption; every gate signal passes on each task; it lands on the preview

requirements.statement: Decisions are self-declared by a single operator, and signed by granted, verified identities when access is enforced.
requirements.notes: D-0016. Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells.

acceptance.given: a factory home with no access file
acceptance.when: two people answer, each typing a name and a persona
acceptance.then: the factory says single operator: personas are self-declared, and the decisions carry the typed names and no identity

acceptance.given: an enforced access file binding a group, a person and a person on one project
acceptance.when: the one-line need runs to production
acceptance.then: no identity, a typed name that is not the identity, a persona not granted and a project outside the scope are refused with nothing recorded; every decision of the run is recorded with the identity that signed it

requirements.statement: Every path writes the same trace to the ledger: who asked, who decided or let the factory assume, what was assumed and what proves it.
requirements.notes: D-0017. Proposed by the acceptance-matrix stream from the owner's goal (2026-11-23): before company use, every use case and mode works end to end. The criteria are the stream's own wording, for the owner to confirm or change. docs/acceptance.md is the matrix; tests/acceptance runs its offline cells. Its expected-failure criteria propose behaviour the owner has not decided; they record a gap measured today, not a promise.

acceptance.given: the quickest path (an automation in assume mode at explore) and the strictest (the one-line need in socratic mode at production)
acceptance.when: both run to their release and compliance exports the strict one's evidence pack
acceptance.then: both ledgers are intact with every gate, the release and the pack; the quick one holds every assumption and no decision, the strict one every decision by name and no assumption; the evidence pack is attestable

acceptance.given: a need filed through the kernel's intake, as the command line files it
acceptance.when: intake runs
acceptance.then: the ledger records who asked and who chose the mode (expected failure today: only the cockpit records them)

requirements.statement: A person can open a chat, give a file if they want, and work out the spec with Rihma: Rihma asks one or two questions at a time and keeps a draft brief beside the chat that the person can edit, says when it is good enough, and the person creates the project from it, choosing the work profile, mode and maturity with Rihma's suggestion; the conversation is kept, signed and resumable.
requirements.notes: The owner (D-0022): "the platform provides also the mode that user can just open a chat and maybe give a file ... figure out the specs with Rihmasto". kernel/shape.py, kernel/shape_cli.py, cockpit/shape_routes.py, cockpit/static/shape.js, docs/guides/shape-in-chat.md. Built: the chat, the draft, attachments (text, Markdown, Word, a folder), create with intake, resume, the cockpit and `rihmasto shape`. Not built here: D-0022's per-answer Inbox signing of each chat answer and the website need-chat hand-over.

acceptance.given: a person with a notes file and a sentence about a need
acceptance.when: they start a conversation, attach the file and say the sentence
acceptance.then: Rihma, as the analyst role, reads both and answers with at most two questions and a draft brief (who it is for, the problem, outcomes, scope in and out, constraints, data and systems, open questions); the conversation is kept under the factory home's _shape/<id>/ and the factory's ledger records shape_started, shape_attached and shape_said, signed, with the words' hash and never the words

acceptance.given: a draft Rihma proposed
acceptance.when: the person edits fields of the draft and talks on
acceptance.then: the edited fields keep the person's words in every later draft, Rihma is told which fields are the person's, and shape_draft_edited records who changed which fields

acceptance.given: no model set up, a model that fails, or one that answers without the draft's JSON
acceptance.when: the person says something
acceptance.then: the chat says that no model is set up and links to Models setup, or says the error and links there, or shows the answer as it is; the person's words are kept and the chat never waits for ever

acceptance.given: a draft that says who it is for, the outcomes and the scope, and an open question
acceptance.when: the person creates the project from it
acceptance.then: the project's request is the draft as a brief whose headings name those facets, so intake reads them as given and asks none of them again; the open question stays a question; the project carries the conversation and shaped_in_chat, the factory's ledger shape_created with the profile, mode and maturity chosen; the conversation takes no more messages

acceptance.given: a conversation left open
acceptance.when: a person comes back to it later, from another process
acceptance.then: it is listed with its title, Rihma answers with the whole conversation so far, and the draft goes on from where it was

acceptance.given: a Word document, a folder of Markdown files, a PDF and an image
acceptance.when: each is attached
acceptance.then: the Word document and the folder are read with the standard library and Rihma sees their text; the PDF and the image are refused with a request to paste their text, and attach nothing

acceptance.given: the command line
acceptance.when: a person runs `rihmasto shape start|say|attach|edit|show|create`, and the interactive `rihmasto shape` with /draft, /create, /quit and --resume
acceptance.then: each step does what the cockpit does, signed with --person and --persona; a step by something that is not a person is refused

acceptance.given: the cockpit with a model
acceptance.when: a person starts a conversation with a sentence and a file, edits the draft, says more and creates the project
