requirements.statement: Enforcement levels per environment and check family: for development, testing and production (Rihmasto's preview and demo count as development, staging as testing; a pipeline's environments are placed by their names) and for quality, security, legal and governance, a level of off, advise (a note in the record and a nudge; the work goes on), require review (a card that only the named reviewer decides; the work goes on) or enforce (the work is refused until the named reviewer decides; an approval is the override, recorded with its person). Advise is the default and nothing is enforced until a person turns it on. The platform sets the levels for every project and a project may set its own for any cell; every cell says whether it is the project's own, all projects' or Rihmasto's default, every change is signed and recorded, loosening a level needs a reason, and a preview says what a change would do before it is made. Rihmasto's gate on a change, the deploy step of a release and an automation that changes something ask the levels before they go on. The project's own pipeline is taken as given: its GitHub environments and branch protection are read with gh (GET only, never written) and shown beside the levels, saying where the two agree or which is stricter and what to do. Everything is doable in the cockpit and through Ask Rihma, by rule.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "how do we make sure Rihmasto is aligned with the dev test prod split if it's coming from GitHub or any pipeline ... in development we wouldn't want forced human check on everything; in testing and production we wouldn't want any critical changes without human checks. So there should be different levels of enforcement ... to what extent we can expect Rihmasto to govern such structure or just take it as given ... stay true to the middle layer vision while helping to enforce the structure." decisions/D-0026-enforcement-levels.md. kernel/enforcement.py (levels, scopes, setting), kernel/enforcement_guard.py (what a level does: the gate, the deploy step, automations), kernel/enforcement_preview.py, kernel/enforcement_pipeline.py (GitHub, read only), kernel/enforcement_chat.py (Ask Rihma), cockpit/enforcement_routes.py, cockpit/static/enforcement.js (the Govern capsule's Enforcement view and the Settings card); the card kind enforcement in kernel/canon.py.

acceptance.given: a platform and a project with no levels set
acceptance.when: a person reads the levels (GET /api/enforcement, GET /api/projects/<pid>/enforcement) and sets them (PUT, levels, a preset or a reviewer per family, or inherit for a project's cell)
acceptance.then: every environment and family reads advise from Rihmasto's default until set; a platform cell reads from all projects and a project's own cell from the project, a project cell set back to inherit follows the platform again; a change is signed by a named person in a persona that may set levels (business owner, IT, compliance, developer) and recorded in the factory's ledger or the project's, anyone else is refused and nothing is written, and loosening a level without a reason is refused

acceptance.given: a project with outcomes recorded under the current levels and other projects that set cells of their own
acceptance.when: a person previews a change (POST /api/enforcement/preview), for a project or for all projects
acceptance.then: it lists each cell that would change, from and to, and what happens there next; how many recorded outcomes would have been different; for all projects, the projects it reaches and those that keep their own setting for a changed cell; and it records nothing

acceptance.given: a project at advise everywhere
acceptance.when: a release enters testing or production, or Rihmasto's gate finds a change not passed in development
acceptance.then: a note is recorded in the project's ledger (outcome noted, with the environment, family, level and subject) and the work goes on; a change in development with nothing found records nothing

acceptance.given: a cell set to require review with its reviewer
acceptance.when: something enters that environment and the family has a say
acceptance.then: a card of kind enforcement opens that only the named reviewer may decide, the work goes on, and the same subject opens no second card

acceptance.given: a cell set to enforce
acceptance.when: a release is deployed there, or an automation that changes something acts there
acceptance.then: the deploy step waits on the enforcement card and the automation is refused with words naming the card and who decides it; after the reviewer approves, the same subject goes on and the outcome records the approval as an override with its person and reason; after a refusal it stays held

acceptance.given: each of the four levels set for a check family in each of development, testing and production
acceptance.when: the guard is asked about a release entering that environment while that family has a finding
acceptance.then: off lets it through without a record, advise notes it, require review opens a review card and goes on, enforce holds it on a blocking card

acceptance.given: a project whose GitHub repository has deployment environments and a protected main line
acceptance.when: a person reads the pipeline (GET /api/projects/<pid>/enforcement?pipeline=1)
acceptance.then: Rihmasto reads the repository, its environments and the main line's protection with gh GET requests only, places each environment in development, testing or production by its name, and says per environment whether Rihmasto and the pipeline agree that a person checks a change, or which is stricter and what to do, with the pipeline's split offered as levels; when gh is missing or not signed in, or the project has no GitHub remote, it says it was not read, why, and how to fix it

acceptance.given: a person in Ask Rihma, inside a project or not
acceptance.when: they ask how a stage is enforced, or ask to require a review, enforce a family or use a preset in an environment
acceptance.then: Rihma answers by rule with the levels in force and their scopes, and Take me there to the project's Enforcement view or Settings; a change is proposed with its preview's lines, for the project inside one unless the question says all projects, and only to a persona that may set levels; nothing is changed until the person confirms it, signed, through the same route as Save

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser at desktop and phone width, light and dark
acceptance.when: a person opens a project's Enforcement view in the Govern capsule and Settings, changes a level, previews and saves it, and reads the pipeline
acceptance.then: the view shows each environment's levels with each cell's scope, the preview, the reviews waiting, what Rihmasto noticed and the open findings, each empty part saying what would appear and how, with Ask Rihma why and how; Settings shows the same for all projects and the projects that set their own; the save is signed and recorded; nothing scrolls sideways and the console shows no error

requirements.statement: Enforcement levels rest on the right facts and never strand a person: the pipeline's main line is read from classic branch protection and repository rulesets together; a card that holds work for a role the person also holds is shown in both Inboxes, counted as waiting on a person and decidable on the Enforcement view, and its words say who decides and where; an approval covers what its reviewer saw (a new finding asks again, one approval lets one automation firing through) and a refusal says what holds; environment names are placed by whole words, an unknown one counts as production and says so, and a person may place it; the gate asks the stage its changes enter and an enforce refusal holds the change; Ask Rihma takes the usual ways of saying a level, keeps everywhere to the stages, and carries the person's own reason; approving held work needs a reason; every decision record has its own id.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "in development we wouldn't want forced human check on everything; in testing and production we wouldn't want any critical changes without human checks ... stay true to the middle layer vision while helping to enforce the structure." An independent check of FR-ENF1 found eight gaps against that and against the owner's standing rules (never strand the person, solo by default, done means verified end to end); the owner asked each to be fixed with a test. decisions/D-0026-enforcement-levels.md. kernel/enforcement_places.py (names by whole words, the gate's stage), kernel/enforcement_cards.py (what a card covers, its words), kernel/enforcement_pipeline.py (rulesets), kernel/enforcement_guard.py, kernel/enforcement_chat.py, kernel/canon.py (the override's reason), kernel/status.py, cockpit/inbox_elsewhere.py, cockpit/static/elsewhere.js, cockpit/static/enforcement_places.js, cockpit/static/enforcement.js.

acceptance.given: the project's main line held by a repository ruleset (a required pull request and status checks) and no classic branch protection
acceptance.when: the Enforcement view reads the pipeline (GET only: the branch's rules and the rulesets' names)
acceptance.then: the main line reads as protected through the named ruleset, with its pull request and checks; the development row says so instead of a merge without a review, and classic protection and rulesets read together give the stricter of each

acceptance.given: a person working alone, looking as business owner, and a release held by an enforce level whose reviewer is IT
acceptance.when: they open the project's Inbox, every project's Inbox, the project's state line and the Enforcement view
acceptance.then: both Inboxes say a decision that holds work waits on IT, a role they also hold, and offer to show every role; the state line reads waiting on a person; the held words name IT and both places to decide; the Enforcement view lets them decide it in place, signed as IT with their name

acceptance.given: an enforce level on a recurring automation and on a release
acceptance.when: an approval is given, a new finding appears, a refusal is given, or an open card's subject changes
acceptance.then: one approval lets one firing of the automation through and the next firing asks again; an approved release with a new finding opens a new card with it; a refusal holds what was seen and the words say who refused it, why and what lets it on; an open card that saw something else is withdrawn for a new one

acceptance.given: environment names such as productivity-tools, latest, contest, eu-west, customer-a, prod-eu and staging2
acceptance.when: the guard and the pipeline place them
acceptance.then: names are placed by whole words (prod-eu production, staging2 testing; productivity-tools, latest and contest are not known); an unknown name counts as production and the answer says so and how to place it; a person places a name for a project or all projects, signed and recorded, and placing it in a less strict stage needs a reason

acceptance.given: Rihmasto's gate judging a change of an attached repository
acceptance.when: the project says the gate's changes enter testing or production, and that stage is set to enforce
acceptance.then: the gate asks that stage's levels (development unless a person says otherwise); an enforce refusal holds the change: the gate's result carries held with the card and its words, the command exits non-zero, and the Health check, the automation and the agent channel say it is held

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma inside a project with its own split
acceptance.when: a person says turn off checks in production, make staging require review for legal, block deploys to prod, advise everywhere, treat eu-west as testing, or the gate's changes go to production
acceptance.then: each is answered by rule about enforcement with Take me there; advise everywhere is this project's every stage, not the platform; a loosening without the person's own reason asks for it and proposes nothing, and a proposal carries the person's own words as its reason

acceptance.given: a blocking enforcement card
acceptance.when: its reviewer approves it, in the Inbox, on the Enforcement view or through the API
acceptance.then: an approval without a reason is refused and the card stays open (approving held work is an override, recorded with its reason); a non-blocking review is approved without one

acceptance.given: the decision records in decisions/
acceptance.when: their ids are read
acceptance.then: every decision has its own id, matching its file name; the enforcement levels decision is D-0026 and nothing names it D-0025

acceptance.given: a solo business owner in headless Chrome at 1440 and 390 pixels, dark and light
acceptance.when: they find the IT card from both Inboxes, decide it in place with a reason, read a ruleset and place a name
acceptance.then: every step works with no console error, failed request or CSP violation, nothing scrolls sideways and none of the words kept from a business owner shows

requirements.statement: IT has a view of integrations and the data side, for the platform and per project: every connection (a project's declared data integrations with their access, data classes and bindings per environment, where it runs, the relay's channels, inbound webhooks, website chats, connectors, registries, paved roads and the model endpoints each role sends its prompts to), each with where it is (this machine, your network, outside, or not known), which way data goes, its health (last check, failures in a row, latency), its credentials by name only with where each lives and whether it is set, and what to do when something is missing; what each agent may reach and never reaches; the factory home's data stores with retention and ledger integrity; a data-flow diagram of the project (sources, Rihmasto, agents, destinations) whose nodes open each connection; Check now, Turn off and a rotation reminder, each signed and recorded; and Ask Rihma answering by rule what a project connects to and which data leaves the machine.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "from IT perspective, you would want to view for integrations and the data side of things as well". kernel/itdata.py (each kind of connection, credentials, locality, health), kernel/itdata_project.py (the platform's and a project's views, agents' reach), kernel/itdata_flow.py (the diagram), kernel/itdata_actions.py (check, turn off, rotation reminder), kernel/itdata_chat.py (Ask Rihma by rule), cockpit/itdata_routes.py, cockpit/static/itdata.js, itdata_flow.js, itdata.css, docs/guides/integrations-and-data.md. A check opens only a TCP connection to an address; every test reaches loopback only.

acceptance.given: a project whose spec declares a read-write integration bound on loopback with its token in a variable and a read Google Drive integration, a relay channel of its own whose URL variable is not set, a platform-wide webhook relay and an inbound webhook source bound to it
acceptance.when: its Integrations and data view is read
acceptance.then: every connection is listed with its kind, where it is (this machine, outside, not known), which way data goes, its access and data classes, its credentials by name with where each lives and whether it is set, and what to do when something is missing (IT approves the binding on its road; set the variable where Rihmasto runs); a credential's value is never in the view; reading writes nothing

acceptance.given: the same home with a confidential project beside it
acceptance.when: the platform's Integrations and data page is read
acceptance.then: it lists every connection of the platform (model endpoints by locality, relay channels, webhook sources, connectors off until IT enables them, paved roads), each project's declared integrations with their access and data classes, which project is confidential, and the factory home's data stores with their retention and every ledger's integrity

acceptance.given: the project's connections
acceptance.when: its data flow and its agents' reach are read
acceptance.then: the diagram has four groups (where data comes from, Rihmasto, the agents, where data goes) with an edge from each role to the model endpoints it sends prompts to, from the delivered product to where it runs and to the integration it writes, and from Rihmasto to the relay channels; an edge to an address outside or not known is marked as leaving; each node that stands for a connection opens it; each agent says what it reaches and never reaches (the builder only stand-ins of the integrations); a confidential project's hosted model endpoint is marked never called and not leaving

acceptance.given: the project's connections and a stand-in for the network that reaches loopback only
acceptance.when: a person checks them now
acceptance.then: a non-person and a persona that may not check are refused and nothing changes; for IT, operations or a developer each connection's result is kept with when, passed or failed, its latency and its failures in a row, what is missing failing first; only a host and a port are connected to; the round is recorded in the ledger with who checked and what failed; a connection not listed there is a 404

acceptance.given: a relay channel, a webhook source and a model endpoint
acceptance.when: a person turns them off
acceptance.then: a persona other than IT is refused; IT's turning off ends the relay subscription and stops the webhook source through their own rules, recorded with the reason; a model endpoint is not turned off here and the refusal says where it is changed (Models setup), a 409 in the cockpit

acceptance.given: a credential the project's connections name
acceptance.when: IT or operations sets a rotation reminder
acceptance.then: the reminder's due date is the day plus the days given, shown beside the credential and overdue once it passes; another persona is refused, an unknown name is refused with the names there are, days outside 1 to 730 are refused; the ledger records the name and date, never a value

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model
acceptance.when: a person asks what the project connects to, which data leaves the machine, or asks to check the integrations, turn a relay channel off or be reminded to rotate a credential
acceptance.then: it answers by rule from the same view with Take me there to the project's Integrations and data (the platform's page outside a project): the connections by kind, and each connection data may leave through with what goes there, a confidential project's refused endpoints and an address not known here said; asked to act it proposes the very request the button sends (check, turn off, rotation reminder), and nothing is written until a person confirms

acceptance.given: the cockpit
acceptance.when: a person opens the platform's page and a project's view (Run capsule) and checks, sets a reminder and turns a connection off there, in the dark theme at 1440 px and the light theme at 390 px
acceptance.then: both views show the connections, the data stores (platform) and the data-flow diagram (project) whose nodes open each connection; each write is signed and answers with what happened, a refusal says where else it is changed; there is no console error, every control has a name and nothing scrolls sideways

requirements.statement: IT's view of integrations and data tells each project its own truth: a check's result, failures in a row and checked time of a project's own integration or environment are kept for that project only; a road's check that measured nothing never hides what Destinations' probe said; turning off a connection that serves other projects too is signed on the platform and warned about before it is confirmed; Ask Rihma's list of connections answers "what does this connect to?" but never a how-to question; a confidential project's agents whose model is hosted are shown blocked until a local model is set, not as working locally; and the data-flow caption counts exactly the dashed lines it draws, a website chat's answers to visitors among them.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "from IT perspective, you would want to view for integrations and the data side of things as well". An independent check of FR-ITD1 found one project's road:demo result shown in another project, a platform-wide channel that IT on one project could stop, how-to questions answered with the connection list, confidential agents shown as working locally while refused, and a caption counting a leaving connection the diagram never drew. kernel/itdata.py (health_key, the newest health), kernel/itdata_actions.py (signs_on, a road's check not kept), kernel/itdata_project.py (scope project, shared or platform; blocked agents), kernel/itdata_flow.py (a chat's answers drawn), kernel/itdata_chat.py, cockpit/itdata_routes.py, cockpit/static/itdata.js.

acceptance.given: two projects that each run in an environment named demo
acceptance.when: a person checks only the first project's environment twice and it fails
acceptance.then: the first project shows it failing with two failures in a row; the second project's demo shows no check, is not failing and says it has not been checked

acceptance.given: a relay channel carrying every project's events and a webhook source bound to two projects, seen from one project, with access enforced and a person granted IT on that project only
acceptance.when: that person turns either off from the project's view or by Ask Rihma
acceptance.then: each is marked as serving other projects with a warning said before confirming; the turning off is signed on the platform, so it is refused for that person and nothing stops; a person with IT on the platform turns it off and the record says it was wide; a connection of the project's own is still signed on the project

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma without a model
acceptance.when: a person asks how to connect to Teams or GitHub, asks to stop a channel from failing, and asks what the project connects to
acceptance.then: the how-to questions get the map's answers, not the connection list; stopping a channel from failing is not read as turning it off; what the project connects to is still answered with its connections

acceptance.given: a confidential project whose analyst, hidden-test author, builder and reviewer use a hosted model and whose assistant uses a local one
acceptance.when: its view and the answer to which data leaves are read
acceptance.then: each role whose own model is hosted is blocked until a local model is set in Models setup, not shown as staying here; the assistant is not blocked; the answer says the same

acceptance.given: a project with a website chat open to visitors outside
acceptance.when: its data flow is read and drawn
acceptance.then: the chat's answers to visitors are drawn as a dashed line leaving the machine; the caption's count equals the places the dashed lines end, in plain words

acceptance.given: a project environment whose Destinations probe failed
acceptance.when: a person presses Check now on it
acceptance.then: the check that measured nothing is not kept over the probe, and the environment still shows failing with the probe's reason

requirements.statement: Each project has a development board, a trace and a developer briefing, read from its records: the board shows the work as lanes (planned, in progress, in review, blocked, done) with each task linked to its requirements, criteria and tests, its commits, its gate rounds and the agents and harnesses that worked on it, with filters; the trace shows every interaction of people, Rihma's roles and agents in any harness as one timeline, each expandable to its record; the briefing, shown when a developer opens the project's board, says which sessions ran in any harness since their last look, what changed, the next development step with why, and only the decisions that block it; a project offers session hooks for Claude Code and Cursor that record each session's metadata; and Ask Rihma answers "what's next in development?" and "what did the agents do since yesterday?" by rule.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): the second brain "is more about how to figure out tracing, how to build up the Kanban workflows, especially from development point of view per project"; "when I click in that [developer] role that I want to advance the project, I want insights about the latest sessions, whether inside Rihmasto with Gnomon or in Claude Code ... and it would tell me, this would be the next step in development". Solo by default: only what blocks the step nudges the person. Hooks record metadata only (as the agent observability hub does): never a prompt, a file's content or the transcript. kernel/devboard.py, devtrace.py, devbrief.py, devsessions.py, devask.py, devcli.py; cockpit/dev_routes.py; cockpit/static/devboard.js, devtrace.js, dev.css.

acceptance.given: a project with contract tasks, some merged, one escalated with its card open, one waiting for another, gate rounds, cells and commits in its repository
acceptance.when: a person opens its development board (GET /api/projects/<pid>/dev/board, the Board view in Build, `rihmasto dev board`)
acceptance.then: each task is in one lane by its records (merged: done; an open escalation or a stop: blocked, naming the card and who may decide it; a running cell, an open workspace or a hand-off: in progress; gate rounds without a merge: in review; otherwise planned, with the tasks it waits for); each card carries its requirements, its criteria with given, when and then, the tests of its last round that name them, the commits that name it or that its rounds judged (from repo.git, marked whether main holds them), its gate rounds and the agents and harnesses that worked on it; changes waiting a decision, blocking cards, open workspaces, hand-offs and open outside sessions are cards too; the filters offered are the lanes, harnesses and requirements present; without a repository the commits say not measured with why and how; reading writes nothing

acceptance.given: a project whose ledger and agent channel hold people's decisions, Rihma's model runs, cells, gate rounds, MCP writes and outside sessions
acceptance.when: a person opens its trace (GET /api/projects/<pid>/dev/trace, the Trace view in Agents, `rihmasto dev trace`) with or without a window, who, harness or task
acceptance.then: every interaction is one item, newest first, saying when, who (a person with their persona, Rihma in a role with its model, an agent with its harness and operator, an automation or the system), a short line of what, and its task; each item carries its record (a ledger record without holdout details, or the channel message), and a channel post is shown once (its channel_posted ledger line is left out); the counts by who and the filters offered come from the records

acceptance.given: a developer who opens a project's board, with work since their last look
acceptance.when: the briefing is read (GET /api/projects/<pid>/dev/briefing, `rihmasto dev brief`) and they press Got it (POST /api/projects/<pid>/dev/seen, signed)
acceptance.then: the briefing counts from their last look (else the last 7 days) and lists the latest sessions in any harness (builder cells, outside sessions, agents in the channel, MCP writes) by harness, what changed (gate rounds passed and failed, tasks merged, the newest round's tests, whether the requirements were compiled again), one next development step with why and the control that does it, chosen in a fixed order (a decision that blocks a task, an open session or work in progress, a failed round, the first task ready to start, then what is left when all is merged), and only the decisions that block that step; Got it records dev_looked with the person and persona in the ledger and the next briefing counts from it; a non-person is refused and records nothing

acceptance.given: a developer who installs a project's session hooks (GET /api/projects/<pid>/dev/hooks, `rihmasto dev hooks`) in a repository and works there with Claude Code or Cursor
acceptance.when: a session starts and ends
acceptance.then: the hooks are a small script and the configuration for Claude Code (SessionStart and SessionEnd in .claude/settings.json) and Cursor (beforeSubmitPrompt and stop in .cursor/hooks.json), shown to copy or download, never written by Rihmasto; each start and end is recorded in the project's dev_sessions.json and in the ledger as dev_session_recorded, signed by the named operator, with metadata only (the session id, the harness, the branch, the head and, at the end, the commits and changed files since the start and the task ids the commits name); a second start of the same session is not recorded again and a second end updates the first; a bad session id, branch, head or count, an unknown harness and a non-person are refused; a hook that fails says what to do on its error output and never stops the agent

acceptance.given: a person in Ask Rihma on a project's page
acceptance.when: they ask "what's next in development?" or "what did the agents do since yesterday?"
acceptance.then: the first is answered by rule from the briefing (the next step and why, what blocks it or that nothing does, the latest sessions) with Take me there to the Board; the second from the trace of the window it names (since yesterday or today: 24 hours; this week: 7 days; since my last look) counted by harness with the newest, with Take me there to the Trace; inside a project only (outside one, the other rules answer: FR-DEV2); no model is asked and nothing is recorded

acceptance.given: a developer and a business owner in the cockpit at 1440 and 390 pixels wide, in the dark and the light theme
acceptance.when: they open a project's Board (Build) and Trace (Agents), filter them and expand a card and a record
acceptance.then: the Board is the developer's first view in Build and shows the briefing above the lanes; the Trace shows the timeline, its filters and the session hooks; every empty state says what would appear and how, with Ask Rihma why; the words follow the reader (a business owner meets no unexplained jargon); no console error and nothing scrolls sideways

requirements.statement: The development board, trace and briefing keep what was there before and do what the owner asked: Ask Rihma's development rules answer only questions that name development or agents in a project, and others get the answers they had; a session is one start and one end whatever the harness sends per turn, its counts covering the whole session; a developer pressing Advance gets the developer briefing; the trace refuses a window it does not take, saying what to give; and every trace line names what it is about.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "when I click in that [developer] role that I want to advance the project, I want insights about the latest sessions, whether inside Rihmasto with Gnomon or in Claude Code ... and it would tell me, this would be the next step in development". An independent check of FR-DEV1 found the rules capturing broad questions, Cursor's per-turn hooks multiplying sessions, Advance without the briefing, a window compared as text and a decision line saying None. kernel/devask.py, devsessions.py, devtrace.py; cockpit/dev_routes.py; cockpit/static/devadvance.js.

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma is asked, outside a project or in one, a question that only sounds like development: "brief me", "what happened since yesterday?", "what did the agents do?", "who worked on this?", "who approved this release? who worked on the security review"
acceptance.when: it is asked from the home or a project, as any persona
acceptance.then: the development rules give way: the answer is the one the other rules give (Review, Shape it in chat, the Ledger), never a dead end saying to open a project; inside a project, questions that name development or agents outright ("what's next in development?", "what should I build next?", "what did the agents do since yesterday?") are still answered by rule from the briefing and the trace, with Take me there

acceptance.given: a Cursor conversation of three turns, each sending beforeSubmitPrompt and stop with the same conversation id, with commits between them
acceptance.when: the session hook records each turn
acceptance.then: the project keeps one start and one end for the session and the ledger two dev_session_recorded entries; a start after the end marks the session resumed (open on the board again) and is not recorded again; the end's commits and changed files count from the session's first start, so they cover the whole session; the trace line of the end shows those whole-session counts

acceptance.given: a person acting as a developer on a project
acceptance.when: they press Advance (the header button or the Advance panel)
acceptance.then: the run starts as before and the developer briefing opens in a dialog: the next development step with why, only the decisions that block it, the latest sessions since their last look, what changed, Got it and a link to the Board; a person in another persona sees no dialog; Got it is called Got it everywhere: the trace says "Read the development briefing (Got it)"

acceptance.given: a project's trace
acceptance.when: it is asked for a window that is not 24h, 7d, 30d, all or a time (GET /api/projects/<pid>/dev/trace?window=, `rihmasto dev trace --window`)
acceptance.then: it is refused (400, or exit 2 on the command line) saying which windows it takes and giving a time as an example, never compared as text; a time with or without a zone counts from that moment

acceptance.given: a decision that answers a card-less item, such as a question
acceptance.when: the trace shows it
acceptance.then: its line names what it answered (its refs, else the decision's id), never "None"

requirements.statement: An AI architect persona and an Agent operations view, across every project (the sidebar) and per project (the Agents capsule): per agent role with its harness and model, the runs, tokens in and out, priced cost, latency, tool calls and tool latency, the harness overhead, the context packs against their budgets with Gnomon's compression findings and context evals, context drift, the agent observability hub's recorded figures and trends over time, drawn as real charts with a table twin and drill-down from any figure to the runs behind it; an Optimise audit that proposes concrete optimisations by rule from these records, each with its expected saving and a way to act on it or file it as a change, recorded in the ledger when a person records it; and Ask Rihma answering how much the agents cost, where tokens can be cut and which tool is slow, by rule. What is not measured says so and how to measure it, never zero.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "one clear view would also have to be like not developer but AI architect ... observe the performance of agents ... token usage, context drift, latency in tool usage, the harness overhead and whatever we measure by Gnomon ... run audits for the agentic operations in a platform and per project context to assess ways to optimize context, tool usage, token usage efficiency, costs". kernel/agentops.py (the read model), kernel/agentops_more.py (tools from Gnomon's trails, overhead, context), kernel/agentops_optimise.py (the rules), kernel/agentops_actions.py (read, record, file a change), kernel/agentops_chat.py (Ask Rihma), cockpit/agentops_routes.py, cockpit/static/agentops.js and agentops_charts.js (lines and a heatmap), docs/guides/agent-operations.md.

acceptance.given: agent runs in a project's ledger (Rihma's roles as model_run, Gnomon's builder cells as gnomon_run, a coding agent's run through its harness) and Gnomon's audit trail of a run in the lanes
acceptance.when: a person opens Agent operations for the project
acceptance.then: the runs are grouped per role, harness and model with runs, tokens in and out, priced cost, median and 90th percentile seconds, tool calls and failures; each tool's calls and latency are read from the trail; every run is listed for the drill-down; a figure with nothing behind it (no runs, no price, no duration, no trail) is null with why and how to measure it, and a total with one unpriced run is not measured with the priced part beside it

acceptance.given: agent runs in several projects over several days
acceptance.when: the platform view is read
acceptance.then: it covers every project the person sees and Rihmasto's own canon, with tokens per role and project for a heatmap (per role and day for one project) and a trend per period by role in which a period with no run is a gap

acceptance.given: context packs, runs, records written after a role last ran and a recorded snapshot of the agent observability hub
acceptance.when: the view is read
acceptance.then: the harness overhead per role says the system prompt's share of its pack, model calls per run, the cached share and Gnomon's trims; context drift says per project and role when it last ran and how many records it was not given were written since (fresh or behind); the hub's sessions, unrecovered failures and reworked files are shown when recorded, else not measured with how

acceptance.given: a pack over its budget, a line said twice, conventions sent to a role that does not need them, a part that defeats the prompt cache, a role with little cached input, a cheaper model the role evals score within two points, a tool with a median of two seconds or more, and a task that needed three rounds
acceptance.when: the Optimise audit runs
acceptance.then: each rule proposes one concrete change with a stable id, its expected saving in tokens, cost or seconds with its basis (cost not measured when the runs are not priced) and the place to act (the Context view, Models, the task, the runs), largest saving first

acceptance.given: the Optimise audit's proposals
acceptance.when: a named person records the audit, or files a proposal as a change
acceptance.then: the audit is kept as agent_ops_audited in the project's ledger (Rihmasto's own for the platform) with each proposal and its saving, signed; the proposal becomes a change card in the Inbox with its expected saving, recorded as agent_ops_change_filed, and filing it again answers with the same card; a non-person, a persona that does not audit agents and a proposal that no longer applies are refused

acceptance.given: a person in Ask Rihma, with or without an assistant model
acceptance.when: they ask how much the agents cost, where tokens can be cut, which tool is slow, or about context drift and harness overhead
acceptance.then: the answer comes by rule from the same read model with Take me there to Agent operations (the project's or the platform's); a question about cutting proposes filing the largest proposal as a change and recording the audit, each confirmed by the person; nothing recorded says not measured and how

acceptance.given: the cockpit's persona menu, lenses, capsules, map and chat parity
acceptance.when: a person chooses the AI architect persona
acceptance.then: the AI architect has its label, technical words and the Insight lens with Agent operations first, opens a project in the Agents capsule on Agent operations, and the view, its controls, its routes (with the persona each write needs) and Ask Rihma's operations are registered

acceptance.given: the cockpit
acceptance.when: GET /api/agent-ops, GET /api/projects/<pid>/agent-ops and the two writes are called
acceptance.then: the reads answer the read model with its proposals and nothing internal, a bad window is 400 and an unknown project 404; the audit and a change are signed, and refused (403) for a persona that does not audit agents

acceptance.given: a home with agent runs, in a real browser at 1440 and 390 pixels, dark and light
acceptance.when: the AI architect opens Agent operations in the sidebar and in a project, selects a figure and records the audit

requirements.statement: Agent operations, fixed after its independent check: the context packs are read once while nothing they are built from changed, so opening the view, switching its period and Ask Rihma's cut question stay quick; Ask Rihma's drift answer says the harness overhead or that it is not measured and how; only questions about the agents' tokens, costs or context are answered by rule before the model; how to measure a figure names what to do in the cockpit or by chat, never a file of the installation, and a model is priced in the cockpit (Price a model) and by Ask Rihma, signed, so its runs' cost is measured; a value alone on its line in a chart is drawn as a dot.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "one clear view would also have to be like not developer but AI architect ... observe the performance of agents ... token usage, context drift, latency in tool usage, the harness overhead ..."; and (2026-11-24): "when you know how it happens I can also do it on a UIX level or by agent request on chat." The check found the platform view took 3.3 s for three projects (about 150 git processes), the drift answer left the overhead out, 'save the context of this project' and 'what does the ai architect persona do' were taken over by rule, how-to-measure text named kernel/prices.json and other source files, and the builder's single day of tokens was invisible on the trend. kernel/git_memo.py (main read once per commit), kernel/insight.py (one git grep for main's test names), kernel/agentops_cache.py (a project's audit kept while unchanged), kernel/agentops_prices.py and kernel/agentops_price_chat.py (pricing a model), cockpit/static/agentops_prices.js (the Prices card), cockpit/static/agentops_charts.js (lone values as dots).

requirements.statement: Agent operations, Who acted and Ask Rihma, fixed after the AI architect's acceptance test: every builder round is an agent run with its tool calls; a run's harness comes from its own record, so a stand-in is never labelled Gnomon's lane; every build attempt in the ledger is listed with its gate; a demo home keeps its own lanes and the map assistant; the AI architect's questions reach Agent operations, Optimise and the Agent channel by rule; overhead answers name every role, the largest first; Optimise ranks by the saving over the period and merges one pack's reorderings; runs without tokens are said apart from a model without a price; Home's Spend reads the same runs and prices; a price proposal is labelled for every project; a zero duration is not measured; each run carries the gate it fed; the header counts every open card; and Ask Rihma suggests the AI architect's own questions.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "one clear view would also have to be like not developer but AI architect ... observe the performance of agents"; the acceptance test of the AI architect persona on the demo home found the builder missing from Agent operations, scripted verifier runs labelled as Gnomon's lane, failed rounds missing from Who acted, a demo cockpit touching ~/gf-lanes, misrouted chat questions, a cut-off overhead answer, per-call savings headlined, a misleading prices banner, Home's Spend on another table, a price proposal labelled for one project, 0 ms latencies, passed verdicts on failed gates, a header count below the Inbox's and generic suggestions. kernel/agentops_runs.py (builder rounds and the gate each run fed), kernel/demo_home.py (a demo home kept self-contained).

requirements.statement: Rihmasto never leaves a person lost. Every empty state, every value that is not measured, every error box and every failed action carries Why? Ask Rihma, which opens Ask Rihma with the context (view, field, project, the words on screen) and answers by rule, from a catalogue keyed by view and field and the record's own basis strings, why it is empty or failing and the step that fills it as a button; no view shows a raw null, undefined, NaN or [object Object], or an empty region without an explanation. Every Ask Rihma answer and every run says who acted: which Rihma agent and role, which harness and model, on this machine or hosted, and whether Gnomon's structure (the contract, its criteria, the gate) applied. Harness and enforcement, in Settings and per project, shows what each role runs on and what changing harness does to enforcement; Gnomon's enforcement is on by default and an opt-out is explicit, with its reason, signed and recorded, and never skips the gate. Decision triage (in the UI and in Ask Rihma) ranks the open decisions that block work with why and proposes one confirmable answer that assumes the rest, each recorded as the person's delegated choice; assumption weights grow as work touches them and resurface the assumption to reconsider with its trigger, moving it into Blocking only when it blocks the next step.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "If I get some null results on any views ... if there is a missing KPI, missing visualization, the agents of Rihmasto will always get me back on track." "Is this now like Rihma assistant? ... how it's running inside Gnomon and if I change a harness, can I ensure Gnomon is reconfiguring or enforcing its structures?" "I got 50 decisions. Can you prioritize those that block work? And assume me the answers. And if any of the assumptions grow in importance ... I would have to reprioritize." kernel/neverlost.py, kernel/neverlost_chat.py, kernel/who_acted.py, kernel/harness_enforcement.py, kernel/triage.py, kernel/assumption_weight.py, cockpit/neverlost_routes.py, cockpit/static/neverlost.js, triage.js, whoacted.js, docs/guides/never-lost.md.

requirements.statement: Never lost answers right. A view whose own records have data is never taken as empty: Rihma says what it shows instead of a made-up reason, and a view no rule knows never takes the question's premise. A typed why question is read for its subject: a view named exactly, a figure a field rule knows (cost, tokens, tests) with the view it names, the page the person is on for 'the page' or 'it', never a search hit in an unrelated view. A failure asked about in general ('why did it fail?', 'why is it broken?', 'why did my last action fail?') is answered by the error rules from the last failure the page showed, or says where failures are kept. A value that is not measured is named by its own label and its answer follows the value's own 'To measure it' hint. Every run carries the enforcement in force when it ran, never today's. A decision triage's proposal holds only what the asking persona may decide; a persona that may decide none is refused with who may and nothing is recorded; nothing assumed is never shown as a success. From Home the triage ranks what blocks work across every project and offers one proposal for the rest, in the UI (Decide what matters) and in Ask Rihma. Ask Rihma's rules for triage, assumption weight, enforcement and who acted take only their own questions, and who acted on a named task answers for that task. The browser checks measure the page against the device's own width.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "If I get some null results on any views ... if there is a missing KPI, missing visualization, the agents of Rihmasto will always get me back on track." "I got 50 decisions. Can you prioritize those that block work? And assume me the answers." An independent check of FR-NVL1 found the nine gaps this requirement closes. kernel/neverlost.py, kernel/neverlost_ask.py, kernel/neverlost_chat.py, kernel/who_acted.py, kernel/harness_enforcement.py, kernel/triage.py, kernel/triage_all.py, cockpit/neverlost_routes.py, cockpit/static/neverlost.js, triage.js, whoacted.js, docs/guides/never-lost.md.

requirements.statement: Never lost when something breaks. One unreadable project never takes the others down and is named with how to restore it; a write the disk refuses records nothing and says so plainly; runs in flight at a restart are shown as interrupted or still running; a removed project's link says who removed it and where its records are; a run ended from outside, a panel with no usable answer, a relative home and a shared lanes root are each said as what they are; Data and context and Home stay quick; every empty, null or warning item offers Why? Ask Rihma with the right subject, scope and reason; automations, team mode and a bad or slow model never leave a dead end; and no raw system text reaches a person.
requirements.notes: The owner's never-lost acceptance run (2026-11-26) corrupted records, failed writes, killed the cockpit mid-run and removed projects over 30 projects; this requirement closes the 19 gaps it found. kernel/recovery.py, kernel/journal.py, kernel/job_registry.py, kernel/lanes_home.py, kernel/shared_read.py, kernel/store.py, kernel/neverlost.py, cockpit/neverlost_routes.py, cockpit/static/heal.js, neverlost.js, tests/test_neverlost_acc.py, tests/test_neverlost_acc_words.py.
