requirements.statement: The public repository explains itself to someone who has never seen it: a README that breaks Rihmasto down (what it is and is not, its capabilities, how to get started, a picture of the architecture, the tech stack, the data and knowledge layers, the agentic capabilities, Gnomon and the kernel, the use scenarios, an honest status and the version history), an architecture picture drawn as SVG for light and dark with a Mermaid twin, a guide per scenario that says what happens under the hood, a guide for configuring Rihmasto with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode through MCP and hooks, a getting-started that says how to verify what you install, a contributing guide that says how to sign off, sync, test, pass the gate and keep the changelog, and a changelog with a dated section for the declared version.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "review the readmes, how they read, all the documentation, how developers can contribute, check that the branches are protected, check that there is a version history clearly tracked ... somebody needs to install, set up, configure with their agents ... configurations, walkthroughs on document level, on process level, on library level ... starting from blank, existing project, improving, maintenance, fixing a project that lacks governance, reliability, traceability, systematic approach in agentic workflows, or building workflows and automations. README has to have a clear breakdown: what is it, capabilities, how to get started, the picture of architecture, how things work and relate, the tech stack, data layer, knowledge layer, agentic capabilities and how they relate, the Gnomon kernel, and use scenarios: starting blank, what happens under the hood, brownfield, enforcing Rihmasto structures on a project or not." README.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/assets/architecture.svg, docs/scenarios/, docs/guides/configure-your-agents.md, docs/getting-started.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml. Tags, releases and repository settings stay the owner's acts: the commands are handed over, never run.

acceptance.given: the README of the public repository
acceptance.when: a newcomer reads it top to bottom
acceptance.then: it has, in this order, what it is and is not, capabilities, get started, architecture, tech stack, data layer, knowledge layer, agentic capabilities, the Gnomon harness and the kernel, use scenarios, status, documentation and version history; it states the declared version, that it is alpha, what runs for real (the local preview) and what is tested only against stand-ins, that the live acceptance run has not happened and that no paved road delivers an adopted repository; and it links each scenario guide and the agents guide

acceptance.given: the architecture picture
acceptance.when: it is opened in a light or a dark theme, or read as text
acceptance.then: docs/assets/architecture.svg is well-formed SVG with a title, a description and a viewBox, its colours are tokens redefined under prefers-color-scheme: dark, it holds no script, and it names the kernel, the knowledge, data and agent layers, the Gnomon harness, the destinations, Ask Rihma and the MCP server; docs/architecture.md carries a Mermaid flowchart naming the same layers and shows the picture, and the README shows it too

acceptance.given: the scenarios (a blank page, an existing project and how much structure to enforce, improving and maintaining, fixing a project that lacks governance, workflows and automations) and the agents a person already uses
acceptance.when: a person looks for the guide for their situation
acceptance.then: each scenario has a guide with a section on what happens under the hood, the existing-project guide says how much structure to take on, the docs index and the scenario index link every new page, the agents guide has a section for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and hooks whose JSON snippets parse, and every rihmasto command these pages name exists in the parser

acceptance.given: a person about to install Gnomon
acceptance.when: they read getting started
acceptance.then: a Verify what you install section says the installer checks SHA256SUMS, how to read the installer before running it, how to check a release by hand with sha256sum, Get-FileHash and gh attestation verify or Gnomon's scripts/verify-release.sh, and that trusting a Gnomon surface (gnomon trust grant) is the owner's act

acceptance.given: the version declared in pyproject.toml
acceptance.when: a person looks for what changed and how to contribute
acceptance.then: the changelog's first section is [Unreleased] and its second the declared version with a date, a versions table names it, SECURITY.md lists it as the supported version, and CONTRIBUTING maps the repository and says how to sign off (DCO), how the sync pull requests work, how to run the quality gate and the contract check, how browser tests run, and how versions and the changelog are kept

requirements.statement: A person can tell which Rihmasto they run and find their way to its guides, in the cockpit and in Ask Rihma alike: rihmasto --version, rihmasto doctor, Settings > About and help and the MCP server's serverInfo all say pyproject.toml's version; About and help checks the machine and lists the guides; Ask Rihma answers by rule which version this is, how to verify what you install, how to check this machine, how to fix a project that has no governance, how much structure to take on, how to contribute and where the documentation is, each with Take me there; the public repository's settings can be checked against docs/maintainers.md without changing them; and the changelog's Unreleased section keeps its headings after a version is cut.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-24): "make sure that when you know how it happens I can also do it on a UIX level or by agent request on chat." The owner (2026-11-25): "check that the branches are protected, check that there is a version history clearly tracked." An independent check of FR-PUB1 found the ruleset's bypass set to always with no approval required while the docs said pull requests only and a code owner's review, Dependabot alerts off, no runtime version (the MCP server claimed 1.0.0), Ask Rihma sending how-to questions about Rihmasto to unrelated views, and an Unreleased section with no headings. Repository settings stay the owner's acts: tools/repo_settings.py only reads them and prints the owner's commands. kernel/version.py, kernel/about.py, kernel/assistant_help.py, cockpit/about_routes.py, cockpit/static/about.js, tools/repo_settings.py.

acceptance.given: a checkout whose pyproject.toml declares a version
acceptance.when: a person runs rihmasto --version or rihmasto doctor, or an IDE agent starts the MCP server
acceptance.then: each says that version: --version prints 'rihmasto <version>' and exits 0, doctor's report has rihmasto.version and whether it is a pre-release, and serverInfo.version is the declared version, never a hard-coded 1.0.0

acceptance.given: the cockpit's Settings page
acceptance.when: a person opens it, presses Check this machine, or follows Take me there for About and help
acceptance.then: an About and help card shows the declared version (marked as kernel data), the commands rihmasto --version and rihmasto doctor, and the guides for everyone and for contributors with links; GET /api/about gives the same and GET /api/about/doctor the machine check trimmed to versions, problems and warnings; the control about_help is in the map, on the settings page and a read in the parity tables; at 1440 and 390 px, dark and light, with no console error and nothing scrolling sideways

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model
acceptance.when: a person asks which version this is, how to verify the Gnomon install or its checksums, how to check this machine, how to fix a project that has no governance or traceability, how much structure to enforce, how to contribute, or where the documentation (or the docs for contributors) is
acceptance.then: each gets a rule answer about that topic with steps, the guide it comes from and Take me there (Settings > About and help, or the project's Alignment, or Projects to adopt), and 'how do I get started', 'how do I connect Claude Code' and 'how do I bring in an existing project' still get the answers they had

acceptance.given: the public repository's settings as GitHub reports them
acceptance.when: the maintainer runs python tools/repo_settings.py check
acceptance.then: it only reads (GET), lists every setting that differs from docs/maintainers.md (the ruleset's deletion and force-push rules, one approval, code owner review, stale reviews dismissed, squash only, the five required checks up to date, a bypass for pull requests only; the merge settings; secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts and security updates, private vulnerability reporting and a read-only workflow token) with the command that sets it, writes the corrected ruleset body only when asked, exits 0 when all match and 1 when one differs, and docs/maintainers.md names the check and the Dependabot settings

acceptance.given: a changelog whose latest version section is dated
acceptance.when: a branch still open adds its entry under the first Added heading
acceptance.then: that heading is under [Unreleased], which has Added, Changed and Fixed headings before the first dated version, and CONTRIBUTING says so

requirements.statement: Entering any project shows what to do there: a Start here panel at the top of its first view says in one line what Rihmasto understood the project to be (with Correct it), the one to three things to do now from its real state, each a button that opens the place (for an adopted project: confirm its kind of work, review a waiting upstream change, map its own sources, look at the top findings, connect a coding agent), and what Rihmasto does on its own meanwhile; a person may hide it, and it comes back when a new step appears; Ask Rihma's "what should I do here?" answers the same by rule. Every task opens a panel (#/p/<pid>/tasks/<id>) with its criteria, the tests that check it and their last results, the commits and agent sessions that touched it, its status history and Hand it to a coding agent, Start it, Mark it done with evidence and Ask Rihma; the list filters by status and source and updates while work runs. The small last-action and job boxes open the whole log (#/jobs/<id>, #/jobs/cell:<pid>), followed live, copied, opened from Agent activity, and a finished job lists what it changed. The same from the command line and Ask Rihma.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), after adopting a project of their own: "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant"; on the agent channel: "not sure yet what should I expect from this chat. Tasks view is maybe too static? Last action is also small terminal view, shouldnt I be able to open the tasks somehow". Built for any adopted or built project, never for one: the steps come from the project's records by rule (kernel/start_here.py over kernel/next_step.py, kernel/understanding.py, the alignment scan, the latest assessment, the agent channel and coding-agent sessions). A person's done never claims the gate's merge. kernel/start_here.py, kernel/start_here_chat.py, kernel/task_detail.py, kernel/run_log.py, kernel/task_cli.py, cockpit/landing_routes.py, cockpit/static/starthere.js, cockpit/static/tasklive.js, cockpit/static/runlog.js, cockpit/static/landing.css.

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose kind of work was only guessed, with nothing of its repository aligned, no assessment and no coding agent yet, and a project built by the factory
acceptance.when: a person opens either, or GET /api/projects/<pid>/start-here
acceptance.then: the adopted one says in one line what Rihmasto understood (from its README, with Correct it) and at most three steps from its records, most pressing first: confirm what kind of work it is, map its own sources (Alignment's Read the repository), then assess it or connect a coding agent, each with its route and control; an upstream change waiting for a decision comes before the sources; the built one's steps are what kernel/next_step.py says it waits for; meanwhile lists the cell building a task, a running job, the upstream watch, the automations that reach it and its scheduled checks, or says nothing runs on its own with the step that would; reading writes nothing

acceptance.given: a person who hid Start here on a project
acceptance.when: they open the project again, another person opens it, or a step it did not show appears
acceptance.then: it stays hidden for that person only (one line with Show Start here), recorded in the ledger with the steps it showed and signed; another person still sees it; a new step (an upstream change) brings it back marked new since you hid it; a hide without a named person is refused and changes nothing

acceptance.given: a project open in Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person asks "what should I do here?" (or "where do I start with this project?")
acceptance.then: the answer comes by rule with no model asked: what Rihmasto understood, the same steps as the panel and what runs meanwhile, each step its own button that opens its place; outside a project it says to open one; "what should I do next?" still goes to the guided journeys

acceptance.given: a project's tasks from the factory's plan, from the repository's own spec accepted in Alignment and from the existing code at adoption
acceptance.when: GET /api/projects/<pid>/tasks, the project's own payload, or the Tasks view is read while work runs
acceptance.then: each task says its source (plan, repository with the file it came from, adopted) and its status with a person's marks over the gate's (started, done); the board filters by status and by source, kept for the viewer in this browser; a signature changes when a task starts, moves or a cell takes a step, and the view draws itself again then, never while the person types

acceptance.given: a task of a project
acceptance.when: a person opens #/p/<pid>/tasks/<id> or GET /api/projects/<pid>/task?id=<id>
acceptance.then: its panel shows its criteria with each one's evidence state, the tests that check it with their last result and where that came from (the gate round, a test named for it, a repository test traced in Alignment, not measured here with why), its commits or why none show, the agents and sessions that touched it, its status history from the ledger, and its actions; an id that is not the project's says so with the way back, never an error page

acceptance.given: a task a person works on
acceptance.when: they press Start it, Mark it done with evidence, or Hand it to a coding agent, in the cockpit or with rihmasto task start|done|handoff
acceptance.then: each is signed by a named person with a persona that may (workers start and hand off, closers mark done), refused otherwise with nothing written; a done needs its evidence and never claims the gate's merge (a merged task refuses it); a hand-off gives the brief narrowed to the task, posts it in the agent channel with the task in its references and records agent_handoff, so the board and the trace see who works on it

acceptance.given: a project open in Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person asks "what about T-001?", "start T-002", "hand T-002 to Claude Code" or "mark T-002 done: the suite passed"
acceptance.then: the answer by rule says the task's state, source, criteria, tests and last event; a start, a hand-off or a done with its evidence is proposed as the same write for the person to confirm, signed with their name; a done without evidence asks for it

acceptance.given: a background job that printed a long log, and a cell building a task
acceptance.when: a person opens the whole log (#/jobs/<id> or #/jobs/cell:<pid>, from the job, the live panel's last action or Agent activity), or GET /api/run-log
acceptance.then: the log is read from its file from an offset (a long one from its last 256 KiB, saying what it left out) and followed while the run goes on; the cell's log is every tool step from Gnomon's audit trail; a finished job lists what the records gained while it ran, each with its place; with no job named the route lists the runs to open; Copy copies it

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a browser at 1440 px and 390 px, dark and light
acceptance.when: a person enters an adopted project, opens a task from the board, filters the board and opens the whole log of a job
acceptance.then: Start here is at the top of the first view with its steps as buttons, the task's panel opens above the board with its sections and actions, the filter narrows the board, the log page shows the whole log with Follow and Copy; every control is in the map, on its page and classified for parity; no console error and nothing wider than the screen

requirements.statement: The clear landing tells the truth and gives one next step: Start here's step to read an adopted project's repository says what Alignment reads and what it cannot read, and after a scan names the sources it left unread (rule and data files, issue logs, task rows in a README) so an old document is not taken for the current plan; Correct it and every step that points at an Overview control take the person to Overview from whichever view the project opened on; the Board's next development step and Ask Rihma's "where do I start?" and "what now?" agree with Start here, and a question about syncing a coding agent gets a sync plan; the task filters are kept per project and never hide tasks silently; a task waits for the tasks it depends on and for the decision it is escalated to, and a person's done has its own lane and moves the board; the cell's whole log stays once it stops, with what its round changed; a job's changes end when it ended and an adoption's are those of the project it made; at 390 px Start here's first step is on the first screen and nothing breaks out of its lane or into narrow columns.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), after adopting a project of their own: "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant"; on the agent channel: "not sure yet what should I expect from this chat. Tasks view is maybe too static? Last action is also small terminal view, shouldnt I be able to open the tasks somehow"; and asked to "consult Claude Code on how to sync with Rihmasto and what to monitor". An independent check of FR-LND1 on an invented repository found the first step promised more than Alignment reads, Correct it did nothing on the Board, one filter hid another project's tasks, the Board and Ask Rihma gave other next steps, a finished cell's log was gone, a job's changes had no end, a task could start before what it waits for, and the phone layout hid the first step. kernel/source_reach.py, kernel/start_here_lead.py, kernel/agent_sync_chat.py, kernel/task_rules.py, kernel/run_log.py, kernel/start_here.py, kernel/start_here_chat.py, kernel/task_detail.py, kernel/devbrief.py, kernel/repo_structure.py, cockpit/server.py, cockpit/landing_routes.py, cockpit/static/assistant.js, starthere.js, tasklive.js, project.js, runlog.js, devboard.js, words.js, landing.css.

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose repository keeps an old requirements document, rule files, an issue log and task rows in a round's README
acceptance.when: Start here is read before and after Alignment reads the repository
acceptance.then: before, its step says what Alignment reads and what it does not read yet, never that it reads where the real requirements live; the structure map lists the likely sources no role read (rules/*.json with their count, the .jsonl log, the README with task rows); after, the step names the document its items came from and the sources left unread, and says the items may be out of date; with every item decided and sources still unread it says they were not read and how to bring them in

acceptance.given: a project entered at #/p/<pid> that opens on its Board or the view used last
acceptance.when: the person presses Correct it, or a step or the Board's next step that points at an Overview control
acceptance.then: the page goes to Overview and shows the control (never "That control is not on this page right now"); the Board's next development step reads the same as Start here's first step

acceptance.given: two projects, one with a task a person marked done and one without, a task that waits on an open decision, and a cell that stopped
acceptance.when: the person filters one project's board by status, opens the other, opens the waiting task and the cell's log
acceptance.then: the other project shows every task with every status (each project keeps its own filter, and a value that is not one of a project's options filters nothing; when filters hide every task it says so with Show every task); the marked-done task sits in a Marked done lane; the waiting task says what it waits for with the way there and offers neither Start it nor Mark it done; the cell's log shows its steps as finished

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose only task is merged and whose Start here has steps
acceptance.when: the developer briefing is read, or a person asks Ask Rihma "where do I start?", "what now?" or "What now in this project?" in the project
acceptance.then: the briefing's next step is Start here's first step (the same label, place and control, marked as from Start here) instead of "Every task is merged"; Ask Rihma answers with Start here's steps by rule; outside a project the bare question still goes to the guided journeys

acceptance.given: a cell that built a task under Gnomon and stopped, its trail kept in a lane
acceptance.when: GET /api/run-log?project=<pid> or #/jobs/cell:<pid> is read
acceptance.then: its whole log comes back as finished, with its task, model and every step, followed from an offset, and what its round changed for its task (the cell run, the gate's verdict); with no such run it says no cell left a log yet

acceptance.given: a job that ended, and an adoption job that runs for the factory
acceptance.when: its log is read once it ended, and again after more is recorded on the project
acceptance.then: the job records when it ended (from its log's last write, or when first seen ended) and lists only what was recorded from its start to its end; the adoption lists what was recorded in the project it made

acceptance.given: a task that depends on an unfinished task, and a task escalated to a decision still open
acceptance.when: a person starts or marks either done in the cockpit, the command line or Ask Rihma
acceptance.then: start is refused with what it waits for (409, nothing recorded) and Start it is not offered; mark done is refused while the decision is open; Ask Rihma says what it waits for and proposes nothing; once decided, a person's done is accepted, the board's signature moves and the task's lane is done; a person's marks are part of the signature

acceptance.given: Start here, a task card marked done and a task's marked-done note
acceptance.when: they are shown at 390 px and 1440 px, dark and light
acceptance.then: entering a project on a phone the page starts at Start here, its first step on the first screen; the marked-done chip shrinks inside its lane; the note is one block of text beside its icon

acceptance.given: a project open in Ask Rihma
acceptance.when: a person asks to consult or sync a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with it and what to monitor
acceptance.then: the answer comes by rule as a sync plan: give the agent the project's brief and Rihma's tools, hand it the first open task that waits for nothing, and what to monitor (what runs on its own, the agent channel and sessions, the latest findings), each step a button; nothing is written unasked

requirements.statement: A project's agent channel is useful on its own: its head says in plain words what it is for and what to expect (coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client and Rihma's agents talk there about the project; a person asks, Rihma answers from the records and can put the question to a connected coding agent) and who is connected, or how to connect one; when a person asks Rihma to consult, ask or check with a coding agent, Rihma posts the question addressed to that agent, which reads it over MCP or at its next session start and answers with a reply, and tells the person what it did, how the agent sees it and what the records say now, never that it cannot; Rihma's answers carry the next steps from the project's real state as buttons, a question about keeping a project in step with Rihmasto and what to monitor gets a by-rule answer, records are quoted whole and never cut mid-sentence, and Ask Rihma does the same.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), after adopting a project of their own: "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the [adopted] project its not clear what should I do", and of the agent channel, where Rihma had answered twice that it could not consult Claude Code: "not sure yet what should I expect from this chat. Tasks view is maybe too static? Last action is also small terminal view, shouldnt I be able to open the tasks somehow". Built for any adopted or built project, not for one. kernel/channel_consult.py, kernel/channel_consult_chat.py, kernel/channel_rihma.py, kernel/agent_channel.py, kernel/ide.py, kernel/bridge_cli.py, mcp/bridge_tools.py, cockpit/bridge_routes.py, cockpit/static/agents.js, cockpit/static/words.js.

acceptance.given: a project with no coding agent in its channel, then one that posted
acceptance.when: anyone reads the channel's head
acceptance.then: it says no agent is connected and offers Connect a coding agent (an adopted project's IDE setup, else the hand-off) with the setup steps, and once an agent posted it names the agent and its operator

acceptance.given: a person's message asking Rihma to consult, ask or check with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or the agent
acceptance.when: Rihma answers it, with no agent connected and with one
acceptance.then: Rihma posts the question addressed to that agent and answers with what it did, how the agent sees it (rihma_channel_read, the session-start hook) and what the records say now, or with no agent connected how to connect one with a button; it never says it cannot consult; an agent's message never makes Rihma ask another agent

acceptance.given: an adopted project with a waiting card and no assessment yet
acceptance.when: a person asks what to do next, and how to keep it in sync with Rihmasto and what to monitor
acceptance.then: Rihma's answers carry the next steps as buttons (review the card, run the assessment, set up the watch, add the project's own sources), and the sync answer names upstream change cards following commits, the project's own sources, its checks and the automations to schedule, by rule

acceptance.given: a requirement and an open question longer than a line
acceptance.when: Rihma answers with them
acceptance.then: each is quoted whole; when not all fit, fewer are quoted and the rest are counted by id, never cut mid-sentence

acceptance.given: a question put to a connected coding agent
acceptance.when: the agent reads the channel over MCP, starts a session with the section hook, and answers over MCP or the command line with reply_to
acceptance.then: rihma_channel_read lists it under asked_agents, the section lists it under Questions for you, and once answered neither lists it

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma on a project
acceptance.when: a person asks it to ask Claude Code something, and how to keep the project in sync with Rihmasto
acceptance.then: it answers by rule, offers the ask_agent operation whose Confirm posts the words in the agent channel where Rihma puts them to the agent, and gives the sync answer with its next steps

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome, dark and light, 1440 and 390 pixels wide
acceptance.when: a person reads the channel's head, presses Ask a coding agent, asks it how to sync with Rihmasto, and follows a next step
acceptance.then: the head says what to expect and who is connected, Rihma's answer says it put the question to Claude Code with its next steps as buttons, a button opens its view, a connected agent shows in the head; nothing scrolls sideways and no console error is left

requirements.statement: A project's agent channel holds up in daily use: a long question never breaks it, a person's questions never use up the limit meant to stop agents setting each other off and a dropped ask is said, each message is answered once while the panel polls, only a request to Rihma puts a question to a coding agent (and with nothing to ask Rihma asks what to ask), the next-step buttons land on the control or record they name and are neither repeated nor stale, an agent's post answers a question only with reply_to and the reply command it is given runs as written, and the sync answer is short and offers a way to state the test command.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), of the agent channel: "not sure yet what should I expect from this chat." FR-CHN2 answered that; an independent check of it then found a long question breaking the channel for good, a confirmed ask dropped by the hourly cap, every answer posted twice while the panel polled, questions about agents posted to them, the Connect button warning that it failed, buttons that did not land, a mention counting as an answer, a reply command that did not run, repeated and stale buttons and a wall of text for syncing. Built for any project. kernel/channel_guard.py, kernel/channel_intent.py, kernel/channel_buttons.py, kernel/channel_consult.py, kernel/channel_consult_chat.py, kernel/channel_rihma.py, kernel/adopted_state.py, cockpit/bridge_routes.py, cockpit/static/agents.js, cockpit/static/assistant.js, cockpit/static/app.js, cockpit/static/adopted.js.

acceptance.given: a person's message asking a coding agent about a pasted log, up to the channel's 8,000 characters
acceptance.when: Rihma puts it to the agent, and the channel is read again
acceptance.then: the question to the agent fits the channel, shortened at a sentence or a word and naming the person's message that holds it whole; a post the channel still refuses becomes a short note saying why, so the message counts as answered and the channel view never fails on it

acceptance.given: a person who asks Rihma and coding agents many questions in an hour, and an agent that asks Rihma as many
acceptance.when: Rihma answers
acceptance.then: every one of the person's questions is answered and put to the agent (Rihma's question to the agent is no reply), the agent's are capped at the hourly limit, and Ask Rihma's Confirm says what happened to its ask, including when it was not put to the agent and why

acceptance.given: a person's message waiting for Rihma
acceptance.when: the channel panel polls while Rihma answers it, with a model and without one
acceptance.then: Rihma answers it exactly once

acceptance.given: messages that mention an agent without asking Rihma to ask it, and a request with nothing to ask
acceptance.when: Rihma answers them
acceptance.then: only a request to Rihma (at the start of a sentence, after at most a greeting, Rihma's name, please or can you) puts a question to an agent; questions about asking agents are answered as questions to Rihma; with nothing left to ask Rihma asks the person what to ask and posts nothing to the agent, in the channel and in Ask Rihma

acceptance.given: an adopted project with no coding agent connected
acceptance.when: a person presses Connect a coding agent
acceptance.then: it opens the AI tools view on the Work on it from your IDE card, focused, with no warning

acceptance.given: a Rihma answer whose next steps name a control or a record
acceptance.when: a person presses one
acceptance.then: a step naming a control lands on it highlighted, as Ask Rihma's Take me there does, and a step about a question or a card opens its view focused on it

acceptance.given: a question put to a coding agent
acceptance.when: an agent posts a message naming its id without reply_to
acceptance.then: the question still waits on an agent: only an answer with reply_to answers it

acceptance.given: a question put to a coding agent
acceptance.when: the agent runs the reply command it was given, filling in only its operator's name and its answer
acceptance.then: the command runs as written, with the person's real message id, and answers the question

acceptance.given: an adopted project with a waiting card, an open question with its card, and earlier Rihma answers
acceptance.when: a person reads the channel and asks what to do next in the channel and in Ask Rihma
acceptance.then: one button per decision, buttons only on the latest answer in a thread, none for a card no longer open, and the first next step is the one Ask Rihma gives

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose baseline measured nothing
acceptance.when: a person asks how to keep it in step with Rihmasto
acceptance.then: the answer is short (at most 1,200 characters by rule), names the baseline as not measured with the command only tried, offers State the test command (Console settings), and the Overview reads the command as tried

acceptance.given: the cockpit in headless Chrome, dark and light, 1440 and 390 pixels wide
acceptance.when: a person connects an agent, asks twice while the panel polls, asks Claude Code how to sync and presses Set up the watch, then pastes a long log for Claude Code
acceptance.then: the IDE card is focused with no warning, each question has one answer with buttons only on the latest, the watch button is highlighted, the long question is put to the agent and the channel keeps working; nothing scrolls sideways and no console error is left

requirements.statement: An adopted project's assessment says precisely what is worth acting on and what is probably noise, for any adopted project: a secret in a test fixture with an obviously fake value or in a long URL path is likely not a secret, with the reason, and a person confirms it real or marks it a fixture for its file; tests are run per test root and a project whose tests another tool runs reads 'not measured by Rihmasto yet: map its runner', never 0 % or could not run, until its runner and results file are mapped; any finding can be marked not relevant with a reason, remembered, out of the priorities, with findings like it proposed for the same; requirements and tasks imported from documents carry the document's path and last commit date and an old one is flagged before acceptance; and the Assessment view opens on two lines, what to act on now and what is probably noise, with why and next steps, in the cockpit and in Ask Rihma alike.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), after adopting their own project: "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant", and "not sure yet what should I expect from this chat. Tasks view is maybe too static? Last action is also small terminal view, shouldnt I be able to open the tasks somehow". Their coding agent's review: findings from old planning documents, a test suite run from the wrong root, test fixtures and URL paths reported as critical secrets, and "What would make it a realistic picture: feeding Rihmasto from this project's own sources". Built as the general capability for any adopted project. kernel/assess_precise.py, kernel/assess_measure.py, kernel/assess_headline.py, cockpit/assess_precise_routes.py, cockpit/static/assessment_precise.js.

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose red-team scan finds credential-shaped values in a test fixture's file, inside a long URL path, and in its own code
acceptance.when: it is assessed, and a person confirms one real or marks one as a fixture
acceptance.then: a match in a test fixture's file with an obviously fake value (fixture, example, dummy, test, all one character, a UUID in a test file) or inside a URL path with no credential-shaped query or user info reads 'likely not a secret' with its reason and is never critical (its first severity kept beside it); evidence stays masked; Confirm real and Mark as fixture are signed, kept per file (assessments/marks.json, assessment_secret_marked in the ledger), applied to the latest view at once and to every later assessment; only a developer, IT, compliance, operations or a product owner judges a secret, and only a secret finding takes the mark

acceptance.given: an adopted repository whose Python packages each keep their own test root and whose own tests another tool runs
acceptance.when: it is adopted and assessed, and a person maps the project's own runner and its results file
acceptance.then: pytest is run once per test root (each package's own folder, with its configuration) and never only from the repository's root when the root sets no pytest configuration; maintenance.tests_measured reads 'not measured by Rihmasto yet: map its runner' with where the project states its command, never '0 %' or 'could not run'; a baseline that only had errors while collecting reads not measured with that advice; the record says what its test counts are measured against; once mapped (signed, assessment_runner_mapped), the results file at the assessed revision (JUnit XML or JSON counts) is read as the test run, passed or failed with its counts; shell syntax or a path outside the repository is refused

acceptance.given: the latest assessment of an adopted project
acceptance.when: a person marks a finding not relevant to this project with a reason
acceptance.then: the verdict is kept by the finding's key (assessments/relevance.json, assessment_finding_dismissed in the ledger), the finding leaves the priorities in this and later versions, the findings of the same rule are proposed for the same verdict on their rows and settled by a person, never applied on their own, a verdict without a reason is refused, and Relevant after all restores it

acceptance.given: requirements and tasks imported from the repository's documents, accepted or still open in Alignment
acceptance.when: the project is assessed
acceptance.then: each carries its document's path and last commit date at the assessed revision, and one whose document is 14 days or more older than the code's last commit (the kernel's own surface left out) says 'this plan is from <date>; the code moved on since (n commits, the last on <date>)'; Alignment shows that line on the open item before it is accepted, and its summary says what the trace counts are measured against

acceptance.given: an adopted project's Assessment view and Ask Rihma with no model
acceptance.when: a person opens the view, or asks what is worth acting on and what is noise, says a finding is not relevant because of a reason, says one is a fixture, or asks to map the runner with its command
acceptance.then: the view opens on two lines from the latest assessment as people judged it, what is worth acting on now and what is probably noise, each with why, and next steps as buttons (tick the findings worth acting on, map its test runner, check the likely fixtures, settle findings like one marked not relevant, check the old plans in Alignment); Ask Rihma answers the same by rule with Take me there and proposes the same signed writes (dismiss_finding, mark_secret, map_runner), each a control on the map classified in the parity tables

acceptance.given: the cockpit and the command line
acceptance.when: a person posts a verdict or a runner map, or runs rihmasto assessment verdict or rihmasto assessment runner
acceptance.then: each is signed by a named person in a persona that may (a non-person is refused with 403, a persona that may not judge a secret with 403, a missing reason or an unknown finding with 400, shell syntax with 400), recorded in the project's ledger, and listed in the signed-route and access tables

acceptance.given: the Assessment view of an adopted project in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person reads the two lines, marks a finding not relevant with a reason, marks a secret a fixture and maps the runner
acceptance.then: each happens on the page and is shown after it, at 1440 and 390 px wide, in dark and light, with every control named, nothing scrolling sideways and no console error or failed request

requirements.statement: An adopted project's assessment stays precise when checked again: a real credential is never hidden as a URL path or by a word in its value, a secret is judged only by those who judge secrets however it is marked, a mapped runner's results are read where the team keeps them and the headline follows what the person did, only test roots that ran are said to run, a local project's deploy and publish findings wait for later out of 'worth acting on now', findings of the same kind are proposed together for every rule, gaps to close are told apart from noise, every next step is a button in the view and in Ask Rihma alike, the landing leads to the assessment, and requirements, tasks and issues the team keeps in tables, JSON rule files and an issue log are read.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant". An independent check of FR-ASP1 found a Slack webhook, a GitHub token or a value beside a link called likely not a secret, an end user marking a high secret not relevant, a mapped runner never measured since main is never moved by a sync, the headline still saying the runner was not mapped, roots said to run that did not, generic findings for a local project, no finding ever proposed as similar but secrets, a gates command not seen as the tests, fake words outside test files, a fixture mark covering later values, gaps listed as noise, next steps as text in Ask Rihma, and the team's own tables, rule files and issue log unread. kernel/assess_secret_context.py, kernel/assess_context.py, kernel/assess_sources.py, kernel/repo_tables.py.

acceptance.given: a secret finding on a line with a URL, or in a test suite's file, or in a file a person marked
acceptance.when: it is judged by rule
acceptance.then: a webhook or bot URL of a known service, or a known credential format inside a URL, is possibly real, and so is a random value beside a URL on the same line, while a long path alone stays likely not a secret; words that make a value fake (fixture, example, dummy, test, mock, ...) count only in a test suite's files and only as words of their own (latest is no test), never for a known format or a test-mode key; and a fixture or real mark covers the values marked (a fingerprint per line), so a value added to the file later is judged by the rule again and its row says the mark does not cover it

acceptance.given: a finding of the latest assessment marked not relevant
acceptance.when: the finding, or one given the same verdict with it, is a secret, or any finding is dismissed
acceptance.then: only a developer, IT, compliance, operations or a product owner marks a secret not relevant (the kernel refuses, the cockpit answers 403 and its persona table asks for them, Ask Rihma offers nothing and says who judges it), any other finding is anyone's to judge, and the open findings of the same kind (the red team's rule, the delivery pipeline, running it elsewhere, documents a published project keeps, dependency upkeep, audit evidence, open issues of the team's log) are proposed for the same verdict, the answer naming the kind or saying none is like it

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose own test command is stated in its instructions, with a runner mapped or not
acceptance.when: it is assessed, the runner is mapped, its results file is committed upstream and synced, and it is assessed again
acceptance.then: a project's gates command counts as its test command and is named with its file; the kernel's own run is said as it was (once, at adoption, its revision and verdict), never 'did not pass at this revision'; after mapping the headline says to assess again, never that the runner is not mapped; when the results file is nowhere the reason says to commit it, Sync the upstream and assess again; and once synced the file is read from the upstream's head as the test run, the evidence naming the drift card that brings it into main

acceptance.given: an adopted repository whose packages keep their own test roots and use unittest
acceptance.when: it is adopted and assessed, and Alignment reads it
acceptance.then: unittest runs once in each package's own root as pytest does; the Tests card and the record name only the test roots a run started in; and Alignment's line on what it is measured against says the files are written for a framework and how the kernel runs them

acceptance.given: an adopted project with no HTTP route, container or deploy file and a work profile that is not a service
acceptance.when: it is assessed and a person lands in it
acceptance.then: its pipeline, deploy, publish and team findings read 'for later' with why (a local project) and are out of 'worth acting on now', a person's Relevant now brings one back (in the view and through Ask Rihma, signed), a published library keeps its publish findings, and the developer briefing on the landing says what the assessment finds worth acting on now with the way there, its next step leading to the assessment (or to assessing it) when no task is left

acceptance.given: the latest assessment with tests not measured and plans older than the code
acceptance.when: a person opens the Assessment view or asks Ask Rihma what to act on and what is noise
acceptance.then: the view and the answer carry three lines: worth acting on now, gaps to close (tests not measured, old plans, each with what closes it) and probably noise (fixtures, URL paths, findings marked or put off for later), and Ask Rihma gives each next step its own button to its control

acceptance.given: a repository whose requirements are a Markdown table and a JSON rule file, whose rounds are a README status table, and whose issues are a JSON-lines log
acceptance.when: Alignment reads it and it is assessed
acceptance.then: each table row and rule with an id is a requirement with its line, each status row is a task done or open, and each open issue is a finding of one rule with its severity and line, a closed one none

acceptance.given: the Assessment view and the Board of an adopted local project in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person reads the three lines, brings a finding for later back, and opens the Board
acceptance.then: each shows on the page, at 1440 and 390 px wide, in dark and light, with every control named, nothing scrolling sideways and no console error or failed request

requirements.statement: An adopted or attached project says where it keeps its own requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, test results, findings and tasks, and Rihmasto detects and proposes them by rule and then reads them as the truth instead of guessing from documents: a glob of JSON or YAML records through a field mapping (id, title, statement, criteria, the test that checks it), JSONL findings, markdown tables and checklists as tasks with their status, and test results as JUnit XML, TAP or JSON; each package's own test root found and any mapped command run there after a person's yes, and results produced on another machine imported with their time; a planning document much older than the code's recent activity marked as possibly an old plan and left out unless a person says to use it; a Project's own sources panel in Project settings and in What Rihmasto understood shows what was detected, what is mapped, when it was last read, the next steps as buttons and the trace, with Map, Change, Stop, Read again, Use it anyway, Import results and Run its tests, each signed; the contract, tasks, findings and traceability then come from the mapped sources, marked with path and line, read again on a schedule or a new commit; Ask Rihma answers where the project keeps them and maps one from the words by rule, with a proposal to confirm.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant". A coding agent's review of what Rihmasto showed for an adopted repository, generalised: requirements and tasks came from planning documents untouched for weeks while the real plan lived elsewhere; the real requirements were rule files each with a mutant test, the real tests hundreds of gates run by the project's own command on another machine; pytest from the repository's root failed because each package has its own test root, so "0 tests trace", "coverage 0 %" and "the suite could not run" misled; its findings file was not read. Built for any adopted project, not one: detection by rule, no model; nothing is written to the repository; running the project's own code keeps adoption's rules (offline, a temporary checkout, a time limit, IT's isolation runner when access is enforced, a yes first, no shell syntax). The old-plan rule (14 days older than the code's newest commit, 8 commits since) and the adapters are the platform's; which files are a project's own sources is the project's. kernel/native_readers.py, kernel/native_detect.py, kernel/native_sources.py, kernel/native_tests.py, kernel/native_apply.py, kernel/native_chat.py, kernel/native_cli.py, cockpit/native_routes.py, cockpit/static/sources.js, docs/guides/own-sources.md.

acceptance.given: an adopted or attached repository that keeps a folder of rule files (JSON and YAML, each with an id, a title, criteria and its mutant test), an issues JSONL file, rounds' READMEs with status tables, two Python packages with their own test roots, a committed results file, and a requirements document and task list untouched while the code changed in many commits since
acceptance.when: the Project's own sources are read
acceptance.then: each is proposed by rule with its kind, glob and field mapping and why (rules/* as requirements with id, title, criteria and test; the JSONL as findings; rounds/*/README.md as tasks; the results file; the two test roots with the note that pytest from the root cannot import them); the two old documents are listed as possibly old plans with how many days and commits, not proposed; the next steps start with mapping the requirements; the platform-wide and project-specific settings are said apart; nothing is recorded, and a project with no repository says why

acceptance.given: files in each supported format
acceptance.when: they are read by their adapter
acceptance.then: records give id, title, statement, criteria (stated or given/when/then) and the tests they name, with path and line, from JSON and from the YAML subset such files use; JSONL gives findings with id, severity, status and line, skipping lines that are not JSON; markdown tables with a status column and checklists give tasks with done or open; JUnit XML, TAP and JSON (a list of cases, a map of names to verdicts, or bare counts) give results; a JUnit file with a document type or entities, and a file with no result, are refused with why

acceptance.given: a developer, product owner, IT or operations person
acceptance.when: they map a detected source, change its files, mapping or schedule, stop it, or use an old plan anyway
acceptance.then: each is signed, recorded in the project's ledger and refused for a non-person or another persona; the source is read at once and every record keeps its path and line, with per source the files, the records and what could not be read (a glob that matches nothing says so); a daily or weekly read is an automation in the person's name; a newer commit than the one read puts Read the sources again first, a new commit with a commit-read source reads them again, and the watch's sources action reads them on schedule; nothing is written to the repository

acceptance.given: a mapped test root with its own command and a results file it writes
acceptance.when: a person runs it, or imports results produced on another machine
acceptance.then: the command runs only for a mapped root, only after a yes, only for a developer, IT, operations or product owner, and never with shell syntax; it runs in a temporary checkout and its verdict and cases come from its counts and results file; an import keeps the time it was produced (a malformed time is refused) and the machine's name; each requirement's trace shows its named test's latest result (passed, failed, not run, no test named) with where and when it ran

acceptance.given: a project whose requirements and tasks are mapped from its own sources
acceptance.when: alignment reads the repository, and What Rihmasto understood is drawn
acceptance.then: old plans are left out of alignment until used anyway; requirements and criteria come from the rule files with their own ids, tasks from the mapped rows, and a test a requirement's own record names traces to its criterion by the project's own source with full confidence; the understanding gives its tests from its own runs (the how-to-run gap cleared), its contract from its own requirements, its open findings with path and line, and Ask Rihma's overview says so; a root-level baseline that could not run is no health problem once each own root passes

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model, in an adopted or attached project
acceptance.when: a person asks where the project keeps its requirements, says use the rule files as requirements, use a glob as tasks, use a document anyway, stop reading a source, or read the sources again
acceptance.then: the answer lists what is mapped and when read, what was found and why, the old plans and the test roots, with proposals to map the found sources; each request becomes the same signed write as the panel's button (map_source with the detected key or the glob given, use_old_plan, stop_source, read_sources) for the person to confirm, with Take me there; other questions are not taken

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a real browser at 1440 px dark and 390 px light
acceptance.when: a developer opens an adopted project's Overview and Project settings
acceptance.then: What Rihmasto understood shows the Project's own sources with What to do next as buttons; mapping the rule files, using an old plan anyway and importing results produced elsewhere each work in place, signed; the trace then shows each requirement's result; Project settings shows the same panel without submitting the settings; no console error, failed request or CSP violation, every control named, nothing scrolling sideways

acceptance.given: the cockpit's map, the parity tables and the command line
acceptance.when: the controls, operations and commands are listed
acceptance.then: every control of the panel is in the map with its page and either a read or a chat path, the four operations are Ask Rihma's, every write route has the personas it needs, and rihmasto sources show, map, change, stop, read, use-anyway, import and run work in a terminal, the signed ones with their cockpit route

requirements.statement: A project's own sources are said truly: an old plan is found by the real commits to the code since it changed, root-level handoff notes and gates' run reports are found; a requirement's test takes only its own verdict and every mapped root must pass before the root-level baseline stops counting; Read again fetches the latest revision first and a commit-read source says when it is not watched; mapped requirements and tasks lead to their review in Alignment and the project's own findings show in Health; the panel stays open while next steps remain; stopped sources are listed with Resume; its own tests replace the root's baseline wherever its state is said; and Ask Rihma reads results words, says what is mapped already, what is not an old plan, resumes a source and draws its answer line by line.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "Im still not happy with clarity, when I jump into the game project its not clear what should I do and claude code in IDE didnt find most of insights relevant". An independent check of FR-SRC1 on an adopted project found where it still misled: an old task list offered first because the code changed in few files, a requirement taking a near-named test's verdict, a baseline cleared with a root never run, Read again reading a stale upstream under 'read again on every new commit', mapped sources never reaching the Board or Health, the fold closing after the first Map, 'test results' read as test roots, the root's 'not measured' baseline still in the header and the suggested automation, root-level handoff notes and gates/ reports not found, issue_id and sev not guessed, unreadable JSONL lines dropped silently, stopped sources gone with no Resume, a run-on chat answer, a relative home breaking runs and a trace off-screen on a phone. Built for any adopted or attached project. kernel/native_history.py, kernel/native_guide.py, and small edits to the FR-SRC1 modules, kernel/adopted_state.py, kernel/automation_suggest.py, kernel/automations_actions.py, cockpit/eval_routes.py, cockpit/static/sources.js, project.js, evals.js, adopted.js and assistant.js.

acceptance.given: a repository whose plan and task list are months older than twenty commits to two code files, with a handoff note at its root and a run report in a gates/ folder
acceptance.when: its own sources are detected
acceptance.then: the plan and the task list are marked as possibly old plans with the twenty real commits to the code since (counted from the history over the code's paths, not each file's last commit), the task list is not proposed as a source nor offered as a next step, the root-level handoff note is proposed as tasks and the run report as test results

acceptance.given: results whose case names are near another test's name, and a project with two mapped test roots
acceptance.when: a requirement's test is traced and the root-level baseline is judged
acceptance.then: a test matches a case by its whole name or whole name segments only (gate_law_01 never takes gate_law_010's verdict, test_rule_1 never test_rule_10), a file named as the test takes its cases' worst verdict, no match is not run; and a root-level baseline that could not run stops counting as a health problem only once every mapped root has a passing latest run

acceptance.given: an adopted project tracking a branch that is not main, with its rule files mapped and no watch
acceptance.when: a new commit lands upstream and a person presses Read again, or the cockpit was started with a relative home and its tests are run
acceptance.then: Read again fetches the upstream first and reads the new commit, saying it moved (or why it could not fetch); a source read on every new commit says not watched yet and the next steps offer Set up the watch until the watch is set up; the repository a run clones is an absolute path, so the run works

acceptance.given: mapped requirements, tasks and a findings file
acceptance.when: the project's own sources and its Health are shown
acceptance.then: a next step says Review 4 requirements and 6 tasks to import and opens Alignment, and is gone once they are accepted; Health lists the open findings of the project's own file with severity and their place in the code

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma in a project with a gate run report, a mapped findings file and a stopped source
acceptance.when: a person says 'use gates/run-report.json as test results', 'use the gate results as test runs', 'use the issues file as findings', 'use README.md anyway', 'resume SRC-1', or asks where the project keeps its own
acceptance.then: test results and runs are read as results and proposed to map; a source mapped already is named as such with no proposal; a document that is not an old plan is said not to be one; resume proposes the signed map of the stopped source; the answer's mapped test roots say their latest runs and its latest runs are listed

acceptance.given: a JSONL findings file using issue_id, sev and loc, with lines that are not JSON objects
acceptance.when: it is read
acceptance.then: the id, severity and place are mapped by rule, findings say their place in the code with the line of the file that keeps them, and the unreadable lines are said in the source's errors with their line numbers, never dropped silently

acceptance.given: a mapped findings source a person stopped
acceptance.when: the panel is shown and the person resumes it
acceptance.then: it is listed under Stopped with who stopped it and why and a Resume button; what it reads is neither found nor a next step again; Resume reads it again as it was mapped, signed

acceptance.given: an adopted project whose own test root ran and passed while its root-level baseline was not measured
acceptance.when: its state, the suggested automation and an automation that runs its tests are shown or fire
acceptance.then: the header, Its state and Ask Rihma say its own tests (the repository's root passed) instead of the root's baseline, the suggested automation names the mapped roots' commands, and the automation runs each mapped root in its owner's name

acceptance.given: a developer in a real browser, dark at 1440 px and light at 390 px
acceptance.when: they map, stop and resume a source, ask Rihma, open Health, import results and open the review step
acceptance.then: the panel stays open with its next steps after a map, the toast says the review that comes next, Stopped shows Resume, Rihma's answer is drawn line by line, Health shows the project's own findings, the header says its own tests, the review step opens Alignment, and at 390 px each trace row stacks with its result first with no sideways scroll; no console error, failed request or CSP violation, every control named, nothing wider than the screen

requirements.statement: A person can share a time-limited, read-only view of their work with a colleague through an observer link: for one project or every project (the platform scope, shown as such), for an hour, a day or a week, optionally naming the guest; shown once to copy and pass on (Rihmasto sends nothing), kept as a hash with its expiry, revocable at once and listed with when it was last opened and who is watching now. The guest opens it on the same machine or through the ssh tunnel and sees the views in scope, the agent channel and, following, the view the sharer is on and their latest actions (with a pause); the guest may comment, signed and marked as a guest, and, when the sharer allows it, suggest answers to intake questions that the sharer confirms or declines; the guest never decides, runs, changes a setting, sees a secret or another project, and a confidential project is shown only with its own explicit tick. Every visit and comment is in the ledger. Ask Rihma proposes the same link to confirm.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "it would be really useful to share temporary access to view users current doings in rihmasto as observer, let say you want to invite colleague to check work or defining a project together". Observer links reuse the one-use outside links' pattern (kernel/hitl_links.py): only a sha256 is kept, the token travels after #, the page has its own strict policy; unlike those, a link opens as often as needed until it expires or is revoked, each opening a visit with its own tab session. Who is watching and the sharer's current view are kept in memory only. kernel/observe.py, kernel/observe_view.py, kernel/observe_page.py, kernel/observe_chat.py, kernel/observe_cli.py, cockpit/observe_routes.py, cockpit/static/share.js, cockpit/static/observe_follow.js, cockpit/static/observer.html, cockpit/static/observer.js.

acceptance.given: a person signed with a persona, and a project
acceptance.when: they make an observer link for that project or every project, for an hour, a day or a week, naming a guest
acceptance.then: the reply gives the address once (this cockpit's /o/ with the token after #) and says Rihmasto sends nothing; only the token's sha256 and the expiry are kept, never shown again; the link is in the project's ledger (every project's: the factory's) signed by the person; any other duration, and a non-person, are refused

acceptance.given: an active observer link
acceptance.when: the guest opens it in a browser and asks for another project too
acceptance.then: the page, under a policy with no inline script, frame, referrer or cache, shows only the projects in scope: each one's overview, plan, decisions waiting, activity and agent channel, with every text masked of secrets and nothing of another project, a hash or a session; the visit is in the ledger and the sharer's list shows when it was last opened and who is watching now

acceptance.given: an observer link that has expired, or was revoked after being opened
acceptance.when: the guest opens it, or uses a session it opened
acceptance.then: each is refused with 403 and words that say to ask for a new link; a revoke ends every session the link opened at once, and the link reused after the revoke is refused

acceptance.given: a guest's session or link token
acceptance.when: it is sent to every write route of the cockpit's route table, and to a read
acceptance.then: every one is refused with 403 (an observer only watches) and the factory home is unchanged, while the operator's own session still writes

acceptance.given: a confidential project
acceptance.when: a person makes a link for it without the explicit tick, or for every project
acceptance.then: the project link is refused and says to tick Include confidential projects; a link for every project leaves it out and a guest asking for it sees nothing of it; with the tick it is shared

acceptance.given: an active link and the sharer working in the cockpit
acceptance.when: the sharer opens a view, moves to a project outside the link, or pauses following
acceptance.then: the guest sees the view and project the sharer is on and their latest actions in scope; outside the link it says only that they are elsewhere; paused it says so; where the sharer is records nothing

acceptance.given: a guest on a link that allows defining the project together
acceptance.when: they comment and suggest an answer to an open intake question, and the sharer confirms it
acceptance.then: the comment is signed with the guest's name, marked as a guest's, in the ledger and on the sharer's page; the suggestion waits and is no answer until a person confirms it, which answers the question signed by that person (declining leaves it open); a link for watching only refuses suggestions

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model, and the command line
acceptance.when: a person asks to share their screen with a colleague for an hour (or for a week with a named guest, or to define the project together), who is watching, or to stop sharing; or runs rihmasto share link and revoke
acceptance.then: Ask Rihma proposes the observer link (an hour, a day or a week; the project or every project) that Confirm sends signed and shows once, never for a confidential project; answers who is watching; proposes each revoke; the command line makes and revokes links, signed; every control of the Share page has its chat path in the parity tables

acceptance.given: the cockpit in a real browser on its own ports
acceptance.when: a person opens Share, makes a link, works on a project's plan, the guest opens the link, follows, comments, and the person revokes the link
acceptance.then: Share's empty state says what would appear and how; the address is shown once; the guest's page follows to the plan, shows nothing of another project and takes the comment; Share shows the comment and who is watching; after the revoke the guest's page says sharing stopped; at 1440 and 390 px, dark and light, with no console error, every control named and nothing scrolling sideways

requirements.statement: Observer links keep their promises after an independent check: a pause in showing guests the view a person is on holds until that person resumes, whether paused on the Share page or through Ask Rihma, and the page's heartbeat never undoes it; a guest's tab opens a new link pasted into it; following tells a guest only what the link covers, in plain words, never a route id; Ask Rihma answers only questions about observer links; a guest cannot flood the sharer with comments or suggestions; the chip saying who is watching covers nothing and says so within seconds; the docs and the Share page warn that a tunnel is an ssh login and say how to give one port only; and with access enforced the Share page's read, a platform-wide link and a revoke stay within each person's grants.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), on the independent check's findings about observer links: "Fix every one, each with a test that fails first." The pause is the server's, kept in memory (kernel/observe_guard.py paused_now): only an explicit pause or resume changes it, and the page mirrors the server's answer. kernel/observe_guard.py, kernel/observe.py, kernel/observe_view.py, kernel/observe_page.py, kernel/observe_chat.py, cockpit/observe_routes.py, cockpit/static/observe_follow.js, cockpit/static/observer.js, cockpit/static/share.css, cockpit/static/share.js, cockpit/static/assistant.js, docs/guides/observer-links.md.

requirements.statement: A box a person made compact can be opened for review without changing its size: wherever a card, widget, panel or list can be compact (Home's small and medium widgets and their widget menu, a view's sections made compact with Customize, the agent channel beside the view, the live view's last-action box, the Agents strip's list), the box carries Expand (and a click on its head does the same), which shows its whole content in place, or in a side panel where growing in place would break the grid, always a sheet at phone width; Collapse folds it back; the chosen size stays as set; Expand is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls and the focus stays on it or comes back to it; and Ask Rihma, in the map and in chat, opens or folds back a compact box on screen by its name.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "When I change size of something to compact I guess I should be able to roll those compacted boxes for review?" Compact modes found in cockpit/static: Home widget sizes S and M (dashboard.js; widgets.js cuts their lists, the square diagram and the catalogue), Customize's compact section size (viewcustom.js, cz-compact cut at 14rem), the agent channel panel beside the view (agents.js, compact), the live view's last action (project.js), the Agents strip's first five posts (agents.js). The theme's compact density and the walkthrough picker's compact list only tighten spacing and cut nothing; folded <details> lists already open natively. Expand writes nothing: no route, no layout change. cockpit/static/expand.js, cockpit/static/expand.css, kernel/status.py (live recent steps), cockpit/ui_map.json expand_box.

acceptance.given: Home with a widget whose size is Small or Medium

acceptance.then: the widget's whole content (drawn at the wide-and-tall size) opens in a side panel named after the widget, a sheet from the bottom at phone width; Expand says aria-expanded true while it is open and false after; Collapse or Escape closes it and the focus is back on Expand; the layout keeps the size the person chose; a Wide widget carries no Expand

requirements.statement: A compact box stays open for review whatever happens to it after it is drawn: a section whose content arrives after the page loads keeps its Expand, its head and its name after a reload; applying the layout again keeps one Expand that the head and the button agree on, and a section set back to Normal has neither; two sections never share a customize key, and no Expand is named by its own words; a box made compact twice over (the Agents strip) carries one Expand; a compact section's Expand comes first in the tab order and is the cut line at its foot, over none of its controls, and a control the cut hides opens the section when it takes the focus; the side panel follows a redraw of its widget (what was decided in it is gone, its Expand says it is open, the focus stays in it and comes back to Expand), shows the toasts of what is done in it above its backdrop, shows a list with no cap, and Expand shows only on a widget that cuts something.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "When I change size of something to compact I guess I should be able to roll those compacted boxes for review?" An independent check of FR-CMP1 found: Set up this project, compact, lost its Expand after a reload (setup.js fills the box after applyViewLayout); the head kept clicking a removed Expand after Customize; the side panel stayed stale after a Defer taken in it, with the focus lost; Set up this project and the empty progress slot shared the key 'section', and the slot showed a stray 'Collapse Collapse'; the Agents strip made compact had two Expand buttons; toasts sat under the panel's backdrop; Expand showed on every Medium widget though many cut nothing and XL had the same caps; Expand floated over the section's controls and came last in the tab order; the tests never reloaded. cockpit/static/expand.js (one state per box, kept by a MutationObserver; the panel follows its widget), cockpit/static/expandkeep.js (cuts, the toasts lifted into the panel), cockpit/static/viewcustom.js (keys by slot or class, never shared; names without the Expand's words), cockpit/static/widgets.js (w.full: no cap), cockpit/static/dashboard.js, cockpit/static/expand.css.

acceptance.then: the section carries one Expand named "Expand Set up this project", first in its tab order and drawn as the cut line across its foot; the title, a hidden control taking the focus and Rihma each open it, the button then says Collapse with aria-expanded true; the progress slot keeps its own key and size and shows no Expand; no Expand is named by its own words

acceptance.then: the panel shows every waiting decision with no cap, and after the decision it no longer shows the decided card; the grid's new Expand says aria-expanded true while the panel is open; the focus stays in the panel and goes back to Expand when it closes; the toast of what was done shows above the backdrop and goes back to the page after; and every Small or Medium widget that carries Expand shows more in its panel than on its card, while a widget that cuts nothing carries none
