acceptance.given: the cockpit's code and the contract
acceptance.when: they are read without a browser
acceptance.then: expand.js keeps one state per box with a MutationObserver, drops it once nobody keeps the box compact, puts a section's Expand first, makes the panel follow a redraw and lift the toasts; expandkeep.js (at most 500 lines) decides what is cut; widgets draw with no cap when full; viewcustom.js keys sections by slot or class and never twice; the words come from words.js; Expand writes nothing and expand_box stays a read in the parity tables

requirements.statement: Rihmasto takes an adopted project's structure as given and enforces its own only where a person chooses: each of Rihmasto's conventions is Off, Advise or Enforce per project (Advise by default for a project with its own structure), with the platform's default and the project's own level shown, the impact previewed and the reason recorded; the Alignment and Assessment follow the levels; Where the work went shows per project and across projects how much of the work moved development and how much conformed to Rihmasto's structure, with a warning when conformance dominates; and Ask Rihma answers both by rule and proposes a level change to confirm.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26), on an adopted repository's Alignment view that showed 124 items to decide (96 gaps of tests that trace to no requirement, tasks and requirements read from planning documents weeks older than the code, API contracts): "Code plan highlights 124 to decide, how do I know what should I do with these results? I also feel like lacking clarity of some view that how much rihmasto is able / trying to ingest existing structures of project versus are the tasks highlighted about enforcing rihmasto's own structure? I would also want to understand the impact of changes, not just accept them blindly. ... Do I just spend accepting changes that forces project to rihmasto structure or actually moving the needle with dev. Ofc I can enforce those where I should if beneficial, but not blindsided". kernel/structure_policy.py, kernel/structure_cards.py, kernel/work_balance.py, kernel/structure_chat.py, cockpit/structure_routes.py, cockpit/static/structure.js, cockpit/static/workbalance.js.

acceptance.given: a project brought in with its own structure (adopted or attached) and a project Rihmasto builds
acceptance.when: a person reads Rihmasto's structure for each (GET /api/projects/<pid>/structure, GET /api/structure) and changes a convention's level
acceptance.then: each of the seven conventions (tests trace to requirements, given/when/then criteria, tasks link to criteria, decisions recorded, API contracts declared, commit hygiene, repository layout checks) has a level Off, Advise or Enforce with its scope (this project, all projects or Rihmasto's default) and the platform's level beside it; the default is Advise for a project with its own structure and Enforce for one Rihmasto builds; the preview says what moves and records nothing; a save is signed by a business owner, product owner, developer or IT with the reason given, recorded as structure_set in the project's (or the factory's) ledger, refused for another persona or a non-person, and nothing is written to the repository

acceptance.given: an aligned repository whose alignment found trace links and gaps of Rihmasto's conventions
acceptance.when: the convention is set to Advise, Off or Enforce for the project
acceptance.then: the Alignment view says how many items take in the project's own specs, tasks, decisions and contracts, how many are facts about its files, how many are Rihmasto's conventions by level, and how many are left to decide; Advise folds a convention's items as suggestions not counted to decide; Off leaves them out with a count and why (who set it and their reason); Enforce counts them, opens one structure card per convention in the Inbox (withdrawn when it is no longer enforced or nothing is open; Advise instead on the card sets it to Advise, signed) and names them at the repo gate; the Assessment's README, code-owners and audit-trail findings follow the same levels and leave the suggested order unless enforced

acceptance.given: a project with merges, passing checks, applied changes or repository commits, and Alignment decisions and structure levels in a period
acceptance.when: a person reads Where the work went for the project or across projects (GET /api/work-balance)
acceptance.then: the read says how many moved development (code changed, tests added or passing, features, fixes, decisions that moved the work on) and how many conformed to Rihmasto's structure (records taken in, traces and gaps, structure levels and cards), with the items behind each bar, a plain sentence and, when conformance is at least five items and twice development, a warning with next steps (switch enforced conventions to Advise, map the project's own sources on Alignment); reading, scanning and settings count in neither; nothing is recorded

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model
acceptance.when: a person asks "am I just conforming to Rihmasto or moving development?", "turn off the test-trace convention for this project" or which of Rihmasto's conventions apply here
acceptance.then: the first is answered by rule with the period's balance, its warning and next steps from the real state with Take me there; the second proposes structure_set for the project with the preview's lines and the person's reason (or their own words), which the person confirms in the cockpit, signed, and which is refused as a proposal for a persona that may not set it; the third lists each convention's level and where it comes from

acceptance.given: the cockpit's tables
acceptance.when: the write routes, controls and chat paths are read against the code
acceptance.then: PUT /api/structure, PUT /api/projects/<pid>/structure and POST /api/structure/preview are signed writes in the route tables with the personas they need; structure_policy (on Alignment for a project and in Settings for all projects), structure_preview and work_balance are in the cockpit's map with their pages, the first answered by kernel.structure_chat and the other two reads in the parity tables

acceptance.given: an attached repository in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person opens the Alignment view, previews and saves Off for tests trace to requirements, sees the hidden count, and reads Where the work went on the Overview, Insights and Rihmasto's structure in Settings
acceptance.then: each is shown with its words and buttons at 1440 and 390 px, dark and light, every control named, with no console error, failed request or sideways scroll

requirements.statement: What Rihmasto takes in from a project's own files is the project's own structure in every view: the Alignment and Where the work went agree on it, and only work on Rihmasto's own conventions counts as conformance (never lowering one); each item says what it counts as and how old its source is; the card of an enforced convention is decided by whoever may enforce it; the IDE text, the command line, the headline and the Assessment follow the levels; a change waits for its preview and reason; and Ask Rihma answers the owner's own words about the items to decide by rule, with the real split and next steps, and never proposes enforcing a convention a person only asked about.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "how much rihmasto is able / trying to ingest existing structures of project versus are the tasks highlighted about enforcing rihmasto's own structure? I would also want to understand the impact of changes, not just accept them blindly. ... Do I just spend accepting changes that forces project to rihmasto structure or actually moving the needle with dev. Ofc I can enforce those where I should if beneficial, but not blindsided". An independent check of FR-STR1 found that the two views contradicted each other, that lowering a convention counted as conformance, that no item said what it was or how old its source was, that a business owner could not decide the card they opened, that asking about a convention proposed enforcing it, and that the owner's own first sentence was not answered by rule. kernel/structure_sides.py, kernel/structure_guide.py, kernel/work_balance.py, kernel/structure_policy.py, kernel/structure_chat.py, kernel/alignment_records.py, kernel/alignment_cli.py, kernel/canon.py, cockpit/static/alignment.js, cockpit/static/structure.js, cockpit/static/workbalance.js, cockpit/static/assessment.js.

acceptance.given: an attached repository whose task lists, specs and decisions were taken in by accepting them on the Alignment view
acceptance.when: Where the work went is read for the project
acceptance.then: the records taken in from the project's own files and the facts about them are counted as taken in, beside the two bars and in neither, never as conformance to Rihmasto's structure; only decisions on a convention's trace links and gaps are conformance; each item sits on the side the Alignment view gives it (kernel/structure_sides.py)

acceptance.given: a convention of Rihmasto's structure
acceptance.when: a person raises it to Enforce, chooses Advise instead on its card, sets it Off or back to the default, and later chooses Will fix on a new card
acceptance.then: only the raise to Enforce and Will fix count as conformance; lowering a convention, Advise instead on its card and the change it makes are in neither bar, so following Rihmasto's advice never adds to the warning

acceptance.given: an aligned repository whose planning files were committed weeks before its code
acceptance.when: the Alignment view is read
acceptance.then: every item says what it counts as (the project's own record taken in, a fact about its files, or one of Rihmasto's conventions: conformance) and how old its source is against the newest code from git's own dates, flagged when 14 days or more older; the summary counts the open items of the project's own from older files

acceptance.given: a business owner
acceptance.when: they set a convention to Enforce for a project
acceptance.then: the structure card it opens is in their Inbox and they may decide it (Will fix or Advise instead): the deciders of a structure card are the personas that may set the level

acceptance.given: an attached repository with Rihmasto's conventions at Advise
acceptance.when: a person copies the text for their IDE agent or runs `rihmasto align <pid>`
acceptance.then: the IDE text lists only the facts and the gaps of an enforced convention, says how many suggestions were left out and asks to keep the project's own naming; the command line shows the same to-decide counts, suggestions and hidden counts and the same split line as the cockpit

acceptance.given: a person changing a level of Rihmasto's structure
acceptance.when: they save without a reason, or save a choice whose preview is not on screen
acceptance.then: a save without a reason is refused (400, nothing recorded); in the cockpit the first Save shows the preview and records nothing, a changed choice clears it, and only a Save of the choice previewed writes it, signed with the reason

acceptance.given: an aligned repository with some items decided
acceptance.when: the split line is read
acceptance.then: it counts every item found, decided or not, says how many are decided and how many open, and reads in good English for one item

acceptance.given: tests trace to requirements at Advise or Off for a project

acceptance.then: its headline is what was taken in from the project's own files, with Rihmasto's tests-trace measure said as at Advise or Off; the measure leads only where the convention is enforced; a suggestion's row says it is a suggestion, never 'to decide'

acceptance.given: a finding of the Assessment about a convention set Off
acceptance.when: the Assessment is read
acceptance.then: the hidden line says, per convention, who set it Off, their reason and for whom (this project, or all projects with their own structure, or Rihmasto's default)

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma inside a project
acceptance.when: a person asks to see or be told about a convention ("Show me the tests trace to requirements convention")
acceptance.then: the answer is the convention's level and where it comes from, by rule, with no proposal; a word such as 'requirements' is never read as the level 'require'

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma inside an adopted or attached project
acceptance.when: a person asks in the owner's own words what to do with the items to decide, or whether the tasks highlighted are about enforcing Rihmasto's own structure
acceptance.then: the answer is by rule, with no model: the real split (found, taken in, facts, conventions by level, to decide, from older files), that the tasks are the project's own and not Rihmasto's structure, and the next steps in order (older files first, Accept all in a group, facts, enforced conventions, suggestions that need nothing), each opening its control; before a scan it says to read the code first; outside a project, to open one

acceptance.given: an attached repository in headless Chrome
acceptance.when: a person reads the items on the Alignment view, saves a level without a reason, then with one, changes the choice after the preview, saves it, and reads Where the work went after accepting the project's tasks
acceptance.then: each item shows what it counts as and how old its source is; a suggestion is never 'to decide'; the save waits for a reason and for the preview of the choice made; the tasks taken in show beside the bars and not as conformance; at 1440 and 390 px, dark and light, every step is checked when the next begins, with no console error, failed request, unnamed control or sideways scroll

requirements.statement: Every alignment item, assessment finding and proposed change says where it comes from (taken from the project, with its file, line and last commit and whether it may be an old plan, or Rihmasto's convention, naming the rule), shows by rule what accepting or applying it would do before anything is written, and the Alignment view and Ask Rihma say what to do with many items from the real state, with Reject stale, Defer convention items and Accept from current sources as signed actions.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-26): "Code plan highlights 124 to decide, how do I know what should I do with these results? I also feel like lacking clarity of some view that how much rihmasto is able / trying to ingest existing structures of project versus are the tasks highlighted about enforcing rihmasto's own structure? acceptance.given: an adopted or attached project whose repository's plans were committed weeks before its code
acceptance.when: its repository is read for alignment and the view is opened
acceptance.then: each item carries an origin: taken from your project with the file, the line, the file's last commit date and may be an old plan when the file is 21 or more days older than the code's latest change, or Rihmasto's convention naming its rule (every test traces to a requirement, every requirement has a test, and so on) for gaps, derived criteria and suggested changes; each assessment finding names its rule; each group's header counts its items to decide by origin; and the view filters items by origin

acceptance.given: a scanned alignment with items to decide

acceptance.then: the kernel answers, writing nothing, what the contract gains (requirements and criteria, how many derived), the tasks and records kept, what the gate then measures and how many tests become counted or still trace to no requirement, that the repository is never written, the measured state before and after, and how to undo it; each item shows its impact line before Accept, Accept all shows the group's impact first and asks once; a suggested change says the files and areas it touches, the checks it must pass, that Rihmasto never writes it and how to undo it; a finding filed as a change card says the same

acceptance.then: a head at the top says how many items are from the project and how many are Rihmasto's convention, which may be from an old plan, and recommends what to do in plain words; each action shows its impact and is signed: rejecting and accepting go through the alignment's decide (the contract, the records, the ledger), deferring is kept apart with alignment_deferred in the ledger and Bring back undoes it; weak test traces are never accepted unseen; the repository is never written

acceptance.given: Ask Rihma with no model, on an adopted project's Alignment view

acceptance.then: every control has an accessible name, nothing scrolls sideways, no console error, failed request or Content-Security-Policy violation, and the repository's head and working tree are unchanged

requirements.statement: IT's maintenance view has the typical infrastructure checks for apps, databases, networks, integrations, jobs, models and agents, per project and solution type: check families app (health endpoint status, latency against a budget, version), tls (days to each https certificate's expiry), dns (resolve and connect within a timeout), database (a declared binding's round trip, backup recency, storage growth), integration (each declared endpoint's health, credential expiry, quota headroom), job (last scheduled run, failures in a row, duration trend, output freshness), ml (the latest Gnomon eval and its drift) and agent (tool-error rate, cost per run, refusals from run records), each passed, failed or not measured with why and its history kept; a check set proposed per project from its solution type (web service, scheduled job, integration, database-backed, ML pipeline, agent, game or content, mobile, library, documents only with none said plainly) and what was found, each check saying why it is there and whether its rule is the platform default or the project's override, adjustable on both; automations suggested from this context and a run_assessment action that runs any assessment (code, a Gnomon audit or eval set, a check or family, alignment, the Optimise audit, the IT check set) with its owner's rights; Gnomon's eval sets and Rihma's role evals listed with their scope, enabled per project, run from the cockpit, Ask Rihma and automations, trended in Health, the IT checks view and Agent operations; and a failing infrastructure check opening an incident with its evidence and the remedy where one is known.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "IT maintenance view should include typical infrastructure checks done for apps, databases, networks, integrations by agents. Remember to also update automations that are suggested from this context. Also in regards to automations there should be able to run assessments of any area if requested. Don't forget the eval sets enabled by Gnomon." And: "think what they would be per project and solution type too". Every check is standard library only and reaches nothing it was not given: a database is asked its protocol's first round trip with no credential, an endpoint is never sent one. kernel/checks/infra.py, infra_data.py, infra_ai.py, infra_targets.py, kernel/itops.py (check sets), kernel/itops_evals.py (eval sets), kernel/itops_assess.py (run_assessment), kernel/itops_suggest.py (suggestions), kernel/itops_heal.py (incidents), kernel/itops_chat.py (Ask Rihma), kernel/itops_cli.py, cockpit/itops_routes.py, cockpit/static/itops.js, docs/guides/it-checks.md.

requirements.statement: The IT checks hold up under a real estate: a port that answers with something other than HTTP fails its check and never stops the other checks due in the same tick, the IT checks run, an assessment or the cockpit; a check set turned on for a project that runs nowhere opens no incident for what it could not measure; only a project's own active scheduled work makes it a scheduled job, and a paused automation is never reported late; only PostgreSQL passes as PostgreSQL and a refused port says it was refused; Ask Rihma understands the TLS, database or other family's checks and a phone's lowercase "it checks", and a persona the write does not allow is told whose it is instead of offered a Confirm that is refused, as the buttons do; a setting that names no usable target is refused when the check is enabled and said as not measured when it was kept before, and an expired or untrusted certificate is said as such; a code assessment fails only on a critical or high finding and the Optimise audit with no agent run says so; a suggested automation that would run nothing says what to turn on first, and the weekly eval sets run the eval sets turned on for the project; a refused assessment never leaves the last result beside its error.
requirements.notes: The owner (2026-11-25): "IT maintenance view should include typical infrastructure checks done for apps, databases, networks, integrations by agents. Remember to also update automations that are suggested from this context." An independent check of FR-ITO1 found the tick crashing on a non-HTTP port (BadStatusLine) and leaving other projects' checks unrun, incidents titled as failures for results that measured nothing, an accepted IT suggestion turning a web service into a scheduled job, an SSH banner passing as PostgreSQL, Ask Rihma missing "run the TLS checks", a business owner offered a Confirm that was refused, bad settings passing or mislabelled, an assessment's stale result beside its error and suggestions that ran nothing. kernel/checks/infra.py (NotHttp, certificate words), kernel/checks/infra_settings.py, kernel/checks/tick_guard.py, kernel/checks/store.py, kernel/checks/infra_data.py (PostgreSQL's one byte, refused or timed out), kernel/itops_jobs.py, kernel/itops_heal.py (swept), kernel/heal_wiring.py, kernel/itops_chat.py (allowed, whose), kernel/itops_assess.py (code_verdict, evalsets), kernel/itops_suggest.py, kernel/automation_suggest.py, cockpit/itops_routes.py, cockpit/static/itops.js.
